title: The Explosive Diarrhea Outbreak Is About to Get Much Bigger
summary: Official case counts likely capture only a fraction of US cyclosporiasis infections, and the outbreak is likely to get worse before it gets better.
full_text:
The US’s explosive diarrhea problem is worse than you think—and it's about to get even messier.
The country is grappling with a large and fast-spreading outbreak of cyclosporiasis, a parasitic infection that causes extreme gastrointestinal distress. There are nearly 7,000 potential cases, more than 3,300 of which are in Michigan alone as of Tuesday, and state officials have identified tainted lettuce as the likely culprit.
The actual case count is almost certainly higher, though, because most people don’t seek medical care when they get diarrhea. And even when they do, labs don’t routinely test for cyclosporiasis, says Jeanne Marrazzo, CEO of Infectious Diseases Society of America. She estimates cases are at least double the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s numbers.
“That’s because of underdiagnosis and also because there are cases that are likely to be mild. Many people aren't going to declare themselves and get counted,” she says. Cyclosporiasis isn’t as common as other foodborne illnesses, meaning it’s not included in standard panels that test for several types of gastrointestinal disease.
But for many folks who get sick, the effects are, let’s just say, not pleasant. “A lot of times with diarrhea, you have an episode and you feel better,” says Marrazzo. “With this, it just can kind of go on and on, and it really takes people out.”
Bad enough, yes. But about that whole getting worse thing.
Public health officials have urged people to thoroughly clean produce, and some restaurants have taken precautions. Notably, Taco Bell has said it had “voluntarily and temporarily removed limited ingredients at select restaurants as a precautionary measure.” While that might help those trying to live mas avoid getting cyclosporiasis, it’s not the only part of the produce supply chain that can be affected.
Norman Beatty, associate professor of medicine in the division of infectious diseases and global medicine at the University of Florida, says the cyclospora parasite has unique mechanisms that allow it to lodge into the crevices of other fruits and vegetables. It’s most commonly found in fresh, raw produce, particularly herbs, lettuce, and berries.
Unlike some of the more common foodborne pathogens, cyclospora is resistant to bleach and common sanitizers used by food manufacturers. “Despite the commercial approaches to washing the produce that ends up in our grocery stores, the oocysts can continue to stick,” says Beatty. (Oocysts are the infectious stage of the parasite.)
Cooking destroys the parasite, but because lettuce and berries are usually eaten raw, there's no easy way to eliminate it before consumption.
Bill Marler, a lawyer who specializes in food poisoning cases, says that, historically, most cyclosporiasis cases have been linked to imported produce. But the last decade has seen the US’s first All-American cyclospora outbreaks, such as when bagged lettuce from a plant in Illinois sickened more than 700 people.
Marler described cyclospora as becoming “like pythons in the Everglades.” The invasive snakes have infamously taken over the wetlands of South Florida, outcompeting native fauna and inspiring a year-round python hunting season. Cyclospora threatens to do the same, using our guts as the host environment. As more people get cyclospora and poop it out, it becomes more likely that water gets infected. That in turn increases the risk of outbreaks.
“Likely what happens is, it gets into the water supply that’s utilized to irrigate crops,” Marler says. He adds that agricultural workers typically get blamed for outbreaks, but “this is unlikely to be one lone worker not washing his or her hands, or someone pooping in the field. Something has gotten a water supply contaminated, spreading over a larger amount of produce.”
The parasite is also resistant to chlorine, the primary disinfectant used in most municipal water and wastewater treatment systems.
Beatty says it’s likely that thousands more people around the country have been infected.
“This shows us how easily an organism can be distributed to one location within the United States to multiple locations pretty quickly through the networks that we have set up for food distribution,” he says. “This could end up being reported in all 50 states.”

title: CFTC Orders Kalshi to Honor Trades a Michigan Court Told It to Cancel, Escalating a State Jurisdiction Fight
summary:
The federal derivatives regulator pushed against a court order requiring Kalshi to cancel Michigan trades, with Chairman Mike Selig warning states cannot force a registered exchange to unwind executed deals.

The post CFTC Orders Kalshi to Honor Trades a Michigan Court Told It to Cancel, Escalating a State Jurisdiction Fight appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission inserted itself between Michigan’s courts and prediction market firm Kalshi on Tuesday, ordering the company not to comply with a state court demand that it cancel previously executed customer trades.
The dispute traces to June, when a Michigan county court ordered Kalshi to stop offering online sports contracts in the state, a halt sought by Attorney General Dana Nessel, who argued the products amount to illegal gambling. On July 2, Kalshi asked the CFTC how to handle a related order directing it to void, cancel, and refund certain Michigan users’ trades. The agency told it to stand down.
This story is an excerpt from the Unchained Daily newsletter.
Subscribe here to get these updates in your email for free
CFTC Chair Mike Selig said a state cannot force a federally regulated exchange to violate its obligations or discriminate against a state’s residents, and warned that unwinding executed trades is an unprecedented step that risks a cascading effect across the marketplace. Allowing reversals, the agency said, would give traders reason to fear that trades executed today could be undone weeks or years later.
Michigan is the first state to try to interfere directly with executed transactions, but it is part of a broader fight for the oversight of prediction markets. The CFTC has sued nine states, including Arizona, New York, and Illinois, over attempts to restrict event contracts as gambling, and has filed amicus briefs in two federal appeals circuits.

title: US and UK Publish Joint Roadmap to Align Rules for Tokenized Assets and Cross-Border Stablecoins
summary:
A transatlantic task force issued several recommendations to reduce friction for tokenized securities and stablecoins moving between the world's two largest financial centers.

The post US and UK Publish Joint Roadmap to Align Rules for Tokenized Assets and Cross-Border Stablecoins appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
The United States and the United Kingdom unveiled a joint plan on Tuesday to make it easier for tokenized financial products to move between their markets as both markets open up to blockchain technology. The recommendations came from the Transatlantic Taskforce for Markets of the Future, established by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and UK Chancellor Rachel Reeves last September.
The taskforce outlined several recommendations spanning digital assets and capital markets. They also proposed a pilot to test cross-border tokenization projects, coordinated regulation of tokenized securities and cross-border stablecoins. They also want to assess banking standards for crypto and build policies that let stablecoins, tokenized bank deposits, and other forms of digital money coexist.
This story is an excerpt from the Unchained Daily newsletter.
Subscribe here to get these updates in your email for free
They identify where regulators, including the SEC, the CFTC, the UK’s Financial Conduct Authority, and the Bank of England, intend to work more closely, such as common approaches to settling tokenized securities and whether stablecoins or tokenized money market funds could serve as collateral.
The taskforce also issued a joint statement supporting cross-border stablecoin activity, saying the private sector will play a central role in developing digital money and payment systems. Beyond crypto, the roadmap calls for the SEC and FCA to explore easier cross-border capital raising and to review derivatives supervision, market data transparency, and international accounting standards.
The move comes as the European Commission is reportedly preparing to reopen MiCA to cover foreign crypto asset issuers and tokenized payments.

title: Bitcoin Rises Above $65,000 as Inflation Posts Its Largest Monthly Drop Since 2020
summary:
The Consumer Price Index fell 0.4% in June, the steepest monthly drop since 2020, easing bets on a Fed rate hike even as the Iran conflict clouds the outlook.

The post Bitcoin Rises Above $65,000 as Inflation Posts Its Largest Monthly Drop Since 2020 appeared first on Unchained.
full_text:
Bitcoin rose above $65,000 on Tuesday after US inflation data showed consumer prices cooling far more than expected in June, easing fears that the Federal Reserve will hike rates this month. Bitcoin traded as high as $65,100, up over 4% on the day. Ether, meanwhile, outran bitcoin, jumping nearly 7% to around $1,895.
The Consumer Price Index fell 0.4% in June, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported Tuesday, the largest one-month decline since April 2020 and well beyond the 0.2% dip economists had penciled in. On an annual basis, inflation slowed to 3.5% from 4.2%, the first cooldown after May’s three-year high. Falling energy costs did most of the work, with gasoline over 9% on the month, offsetting rises in food and shelter.
This story is an excerpt from the Unchained Daily newsletter.
Subscribe here to get these updates in your email for free
Energy costs tied to the US-Iran conflict had pushed prices higher through the spring, feeding expectations that the Fed might raise rates, a setup that typically pressures risk assets like bitcoin. A cooler read loosens that grip.
Traders are now more confident the Fed would leave rates in the 3.5% to 3.75% range later this month, per CME FedWatch, though many still expect a 25-basis-point hike in September.
The Warsh Fed signaled a more hawkish path last month, and the US military said Tuesday it was preparing to reimpose a blockade on Iranian ports after days of retaliatory strikes centered on the Strait of Hormuz.

title: 從 Open USD 看穩定幣戰爭：碎片化之困，與下一代「美元帳戶」
summary:
Bitget Wallet 研究員 Lacie Zhang 撰文分析：2026 年 6 月 30 日，Open […]

〈從 Open USD 看穩定幣戰爭：碎片化之困，與下一代「美元帳戶」〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
Bitget Wallet 研究員 Lacie Zhang 撰文分析：2026 年 6 月 30 日，Open Standard 聯合 Visa、萬事達卡、貝萊德、Stripe、Coinbase 等 140 多家公司推出新穩定幣 Open USD（OUSD），把儲備收益幾乎全部返還給分發合作方，訊息一齣讓 Circle 股價當天重挫約 16%、市值蒸發約 36 億美元。本文從穩定幣的獲利結構切入，拆解這場「穩定幣戰爭」真正的戰場，並提出下一代「美元帳戶」的想像。本文為 Bitget Wallet 研究院研究者 Lacie Zhang 撰文。
（前情提要：Visa、貝萊德等百家巨頭推出新型穩定幣 Open USD！Circle 股價嚇跌）
（背景補充：Bitget Wallet 研究院》銀行背後，從 Neobank 到鏈上錢包，一場 18 年金融權力大遷徙）
重點摘要
- Open USD（OUSD）由 Open Standard 聯合 140 多家公司推出，儲備收益幾乎全數返還分發方，Circle 股價當天重挫約 16%
- Circle 2024 年付給 Coinbase 的分發費達 9.08 億美元、約佔總收入 54%，穩定幣儲備收益淪為給通路的「過路費」
- Bitget Wallet 研究院指真正戰場在「美元帳戶」聚合層，正探索讓使用者跨鏈跨幣種持有美元的產品方向
發行穩定幣，是當今金融業裡最像「印鈔機」、但又沒那麼賺錢的一門生意。
說它像印鈔機：你收進使用者的美元，轉手買成美國國債、賺走利息，而使用者一分利息都拿不到，一門可以隨規模無限放大的好生意，這也是為什麼從銀行到科技巨頭，幾乎都想做一張自己的「數位美元」。
可它偏偏又賺不到什麼大錢：全球第二大美元穩定幣 USDC 的發行方 Circle，2024 年營收 16.8 億美元，淨利率卻只有約 9%，而華爾街對它 2026 年的一致預期，也不過 7% 上下。一臺看起來能憑空印錢、靠規模不斷放大利潤的機器，最後只落下個位數的利潤率。
這中間消失的利潤去了哪兒？2026 年 6 月 30 日的一則新聞，把答案擺到了檯面上。一個名叫 Open Standard 的獨立實體聯合 Visa、萬事達卡、美國運通、Stripe、貝萊德、紐約梅隆銀行、渣打、Coinbase、Ripple、Google、Shopify 等 140 多家公司，推出了一個新的美元穩定幣 Open USD（OUSD）。
它的規則和現有穩定幣幾乎相反：鑄造贖回零手續費、沒有額度上限，儲備資產賺到的利息，扣掉一筆管理費後，幾乎全部返還給參與分發的合作方。
訊息一齣，Circle 股價（NYSE: CRCL）當天重挫約 16%。一款還沒正式上線的穩定幣，憑一份合作方名單，就讓產業老二蒸發了約 36 億美元的市值。要看懂這場地震，得先回答那個反直覺的問題：如果發行穩定幣不那麼賺錢，為什麼這 140 家巨頭，還要一起來做？
「印鈔機」的真相：儲備收益去了哪裡
穩定幣常被描述成一臺合法印鈔機：使用者把 1 美元交給你，你發行一枚錨定 1 美元的代幣，再把這 1 美元放進短期美債等安全資產裡，賺取 4% 至 5% 的利息。使用者手裡的穩定幣不生息，儲備資產產生的收益則歸發行方所有。
這臺機器並不新鮮，它對應的是一個古老概念：鑄幣稅。誰擁有貨幣發行權，誰就能在貨幣流通中獲得額外收益。如今，監管甚至在某種程度上強化了這一點，2025 年透過的美國《GENIUS 法案》就明確禁止支付型穩定幣發行方向持幣人支付利息。
但問題在於，這塊蛋糕並不容易留在發行方自己手裡。原因不在某一家公司，而在這門生意的結構：穩定幣要有人用，就得有人分發，而分發能力往往掌握在少數擁有使用者入口的管道手中。
以產業裡資訊最透明的 Circle 為例。它的商業模式，本質上是一家銀行的淨利差生意：使用者把美元換成 USDC，相當於給了 Circle 一筆低成本、甚至零成本資金，Circle 再將儲備投向短期美債等資產賺取利差。2025 年，Circle 全年營收約 27.5 億美元，其中僅第四季度的儲備利息收入就有 7.33 億美元，佔總營收的 95% 以上，它幾乎是一家「只靠利率吃飯」的公司。
而 USDC 的分發，很大程度上依託 Coinbase。根據 Circle 的公開說明書和財報，Coinbase 拿走自家平台上所有 USDC 儲備收益的 100%，平台之外產生的儲備收益再五五分成。僅 2024 年，Circle 就向 Coinbase 支付了 9.08 億美元分發費，約佔其總收入的 54%，也就是說，Circle 每賺 1 美元，其中超過一半要分給 Coinbase。
Coinbase 並不發行 USDC，也不承擔儲備管理、兌付和合規責任，只憑藉使用者入口和交易場景，就拿走了產業鏈中最肥的一塊收益。更要命的是，這份協議 Circle 還改不動。據披露，它不可由 Circle 單方面解除，且以三年為週期自動續約。Circle 作為發行方，並不在和最大分發方的談判中掌握主動權。
因此，穩定幣儲備收益表面上屬於發行方，實際卻越來越像一筆必須支付給分發管道的「過路費」。發行方承擔了合規、儲備、兌付、監管這一整套重資產、重責任的活兒，最後利潤的大頭被控制著使用者入口的管道拿走。市場真正開始重新定價的，正是發行方對這筆收益的長期留存能力。
Tether 為什麼能賺 100 億：兩種穩定幣，兩個世界
有人可能會反駁：如果穩定幣發行方的議價能力真這麼弱，為什麼 Tether 2025 年卻淨賺了超過 100 億美元，是全球人均利潤最高的公司之一呢？
這其實說明瞭問題的關鍵：Circle 和 Tether 看起來都在發行美元穩定幣，但它們做的是兩門完全不同的生意。
Tether 超過 1850 億美元的 USDT，絕大部分需求來自阿根廷、土耳其、奈及利亞、東南亞這些高通膨、外匯管制、銀行體系薄弱的新興市場，在這些地方，USDT 不是一個「加密資產交易幣對」，更像是一種「數位美元現金」。這種需求是真實的、剛性的，使用者需要美元，商家需要結算，中小企業需要跨境收付款，USDT 自然就成為了最容易獲得、最容易流通的替代品。也正因為如此，Tether 不需要向某個超級管道支付高昂的分發費，它可以把儲備資產產生的大部分收益留在自己手裡，並進一步累積超過 1200 億美元美債、170 億美元黃金和 80 億美元比特幣。
Circle 的 USDC 則活在另一個世界：美國合規、機構與交易所採用。這個世界更昂貴，但也形成了另一種護城河，USDC 已經是全球最主流的合規美元穩定幣，在機構資金、交易平台和監管友善型場景中建立起了 USDT 難以替代的信任。
同樣是發行美元穩定幣，Tether 在收鑄幣稅，Circle 更像是在向管道繳租。這不是誰強誰弱，而是兩種需求結構、兩種市場定位的不同結果。差別不在「發行」這個動作本身，而在需求到底掌握在誰手中：誰掌握了真實的、有黏性的分發場景，誰就掌握了這門生意的利潤。發行，只是檯面上的動作；分發，才是檯面下的勝負手。
理解了這一層，Open USD 那份看似激進的設計，背後的邏輯就清晰了。
Open USD 的「野心」：放棄鑄幣稅，押注穩定幣標準
Open USD 做了一件在傳統發行方看來頗為反直覺的事：把發行方本該享有的「鑄幣稅」，也就是儲備收益，幾乎全部讓渡出去。也有人把這套機制稱為穩定幣版「國債返現」：誰帶來交易量，誰帶來沉澱餘額，誰就能按規則分走一部分美債利息。
如果接上前面的邏輯，這件事並不難理解。儲備收益本來就很難完全留在發行方手裡，它遲早會以各種形式流向分發方。既然這筆錢最終要交出去，Open USD 乾脆從一開始就把它擺到檯面上：不把儲備收益當利潤，而是當作換取分發網路的預算。
這正是它設計的關鍵。對 Stripe、Shopify、Visa 這類掌握商家網路、支付場景和交易入口的平台來說，問題從來不只是「能不能接入某種穩定幣」。技術接入並不稀缺，真正稀缺的是「預設入口」：結算時優先推薦哪一種資產，商家餘額裡預設沉澱哪一種穩定幣，跨境支付路徑裡優先跑哪一套標準。Open USD 想改寫的就是這個決策邏輯：過去平台選擇穩定幣，主要看合規、流動性和結算效率；現在還會多一個更直接的問題，我把流量和餘額導給誰，誰能把儲備收益分回來？
這本質上是一種針對分發方的經濟激勵，也正因如此，Circle 未必會、也未必需要跟進：它需要儲備收益來支撐利潤表和持續投入，也仍在履行與 Coinbase 的分成協議。兩種模式各有取捨，Open USD 把收益幾乎全部讓出，確實可能換來更大的分發半徑；但當發行方自己幾乎不留利潤，誰來長期承擔合規、流動性和生態建設這些重投入，本身就是一個懸而未決的問題。
Open USD 把自己定位為「網路經濟的基礎貨幣層」，重點服務企業支付和跨境匯款這類大規模資金流動。它的目標不是再發一種穩定幣，而是成為穩定幣流動背後的底層標準。但目標不等於現實，標準從來不是靠白皮書寫出來的，而是靠真實交易量餵出來的。OUSD 最值得關注的，不是那 140 家合作名單，而是誰有能力把它真正推進支付、商家和結算場景，這個角色，目前主要落在 Stripe 身上。
Open Standard 的臨時 CEO Zach Abrams 同時也是 Bridge 的共同創辦人。Bridge 是 Stripe 在 2024 年以 11 億美元收購的穩定幣基礎設施公司，原本就有一款 Open Issuance 產品，邏輯是幫助企業發行穩定幣，並讓企業分享儲備收益。OUSD 正是這套產品邏輯的一次規模化複製：不再幫每家公司各發一種穩定幣，而是讓所有參與方圍繞同一套收益分配和清算標準協作。
也因此，OUSD 想成為標準，靠的不只是「140 家聯盟」這個敘事，而是試圖藉助 Stripe 這樣的高頻支付入口，把真實商家、真實交易和真實資金沉澱導進來。標準的形成，往往不是因為所有人先達成共識，而是因為某個高頻入口先把它用起來，再逐漸讓其他參與方產生相容和跟進的動力。
往更宏大的框架看，OUSD 正在試圖重新定義穩定幣產業鏈裡的價值排序：
- 第一層是儲備層，也就是最表面的鑄幣稅。儲備利息看起來是最誘人的利潤，但如前所述，它往往留不住。只要穩定幣還需要管道分發，這筆錢遲早會以分成、補貼、返佣或合作費的形式流向入口方。它更像發行方手裡的預算，不是最終的獎品。
- 第二層是分發層。誰掌握使用者入口、交易場景和資金沉澱，誰就能重新分配儲備收益。Circle 和 Coinbase 的關係已經證明瞭這一點：USDC 的儲備收益名義上屬於 Circle，但只要 Coinbase 掌握著關鍵分發場景，利潤的大頭就會被管道拿走。
- 第三層是網路層，也就是清算規則、資產標準和互通體系。到了這一層，競爭物件就不再是某一種穩定幣，而是誰能成為支付平台、商家網路和金融應用共同採用的底層標準。誰站在這一層，誰就不再依賴某個單一發行方，也更難被商品化。
三層疊起來，兩種路線的差別就清楚了：Circle 穩穩佔據第一層，在第二層與 Coinbase 深度繫結，同時也在透過 Circle Payments Network（CPN）、自建公鏈 Arc 等方式向第三層延伸；Open USD 則選擇主動讓出第一層，用儲備收益去撬動分發方和網路參與者。
這就是 Open USD 的思路：把「發行方留不住利潤」這個結構性現實，轉化為爭奪分發和標準的籌碼。不過，截至發稿，OUSD 仍未正式上線，那份 140 家參與方名單，更多證明的是支付巨頭和金融機構對新清算網路的興趣，但還不能證明 OUSD 已經形成真正的網路效應。
從名單到採用：Open USD 落地所面臨的挑戰
網路效應是所有新穩定幣最難跨過的一關。更大的分發半徑也好，新的清算標準也好，都不是靠名單宣布出來的，而是靠真實交易量、真實餘額和真實使用場景一點點堆出來的。歷史已經給過答案：USDT 和 USDC 之後，真正跑出大規模採用的新穩定幣並不多。PayPal 的 PYUSD 市值約 27 億美元，Paxos 主導的聯盟型穩定幣 USDG 營運三年也只做到約 30 億美元，和體量上千億美元的 USDT、USDC 相比，仍差著一到兩個數量級。穩定幣真正的護城河，不在「誰來發」，而在流動性和使用慣性；這些東西，短時間內無法靠一份合作名單替代。
對 OUSD 來說，真正的挑戰同樣在採用深度。一家公司在結算系統裡多加一個「OUSD」選項，和它真的把 OUSD 作為預設結算資產、把商家餘額和交易量導過去，是兩回事。聯盟如何治理，合作夥伴是否有實際繫結義務，決定了這份「開放聯盟」的含金量。
可持續性也是另一個問題。Open USD 把儲備收益幾乎全部分出去，確實能激勵分發方，但也意味著發行方自己幾乎不留利潤。長期來看，合規、審計、造市、流動性、全球市場拓展和生態整合，都是持續燒錢的基礎設施建設。誰來為這些成本買單，是 OUSD 還沒有完全回答的問題。
更難的是遷移成本。讓成員真正用起來，本質上是要求它們把既有支付、清算和資金管理流程遷移到一枚新穩定幣上。這牽涉財務、風控、合規、技術整合和使用者習慣的系統性調整，需要較長時間的磨合。
因此，OUSD 帶來的更像是一次「重新定價」，而不是一場已經發生的「替代」。它迫使市場重新思考：穩定幣的儲備收益到底該歸發行方、管道，還是共同標準的參與者。但它並不會讓現有穩定幣格局一夜改寫，也不會讓鏈上美元自然走向統一。
真正的戰場：不是發行「美元」，而是定義「美元」如何流動
現在可以回答開頭那個問題了。140 家參與者要的從來不是穩定幣儲備收益分發本身那點利潤，而是穩定幣所代表的入場資格：進入下一代金融清算網路的資格。
這兩年的動作已經很清楚。摩根大通推出存款代幣 JPMD，PayPal 發行 PYUSD，蘋果、Google、沃爾瑪都在研究穩定幣整合；據《華爾街日報》報導，摩根大通、花旗、美國銀行、富國銀行還計畫在 2027 年上半年，透過共同擁有的清算機構 The Clearing House 推出聯合代幣化存款網路。它們圖的都不是國債利息，而是更底層的三件事：繞開舊清算軌道，抓住帳戶和資料，參與下一代支付標準的制定。
對支付公司和銀行來說，穩定幣與其說是一門新生意，不如說是一張門票。跨境匯款過去要經過代理行網路，耗時兩三天，費用層層疊加；穩定幣把這條路徑壓縮到幾秒鐘、接近零成本。手續費、外匯和利差原本是支付產業最重要的收入支柱，而穩定幣正在一根根拆掉它們。參與 OUSD 也好，發行 PYUSD 也好，做銀行聯合存款網路也好，本質上既是進攻，也是防守：與其被別人用穩定幣重寫支付規則，不如自己先坐上牌桌。
但當人人都想上桌，另一個問題也隨之出現：桌上的「美元」越來越多了。
今天的鏈上美元已經不是一種資產。USDT、USDC、OUSD、PYUSD、USDG、JPMD，以及未來可能出現的銀行聯合存款代幣，都在爭奪自己的使用場景；而每一種穩定幣又可能同時存在於 Solana、Base、Polygon、Ethereum 等多條鏈上。同一個「美元」，被拆成幾十種代幣，散落在不同鏈、不同帳戶、不同流動性池裡。
對普通使用者和企業來說，這會變成一個很現實的問題：我到底該持有哪一種美元？我手裡的這種美元，能不能付給一個只接受另一種美元的人？
所以，穩定幣競爭走到後面，真正稀缺的未必是發行能力，也未必是某一個單點管道，而是讓不同美元彼此可換、可用、可結算的那一層，也就是聚合、路由和清算的流動性層。
這也是 OUSD 之外更大的機會。穩定幣越多，碎片化越嚴重；碎片化越嚴重，使用者越需要一個把複雜性藏到後臺的帳戶入口。就像今天使用者使用微信支付、支付寶時，並不太會關心錢包餘額背後是哪家銀行的存款，未來使用者使用鏈上美元時，也不應該被迫理解自己手裡到底是 USDT、USDC、OUSD，還是某條鏈上的某個封裝版本。
而這一層，正是鏈上錢包和帳戶最接近的位置。
一個能夠同時持有、兌換、路由並結算多種美元資產的錢包，可以把發行方之間的碎片化競爭，重新抽象成使用者眼裡的「一個美元」。碎片化對發行方來說是戰爭，對帳戶層來說卻是機會：誰能把散落在不同鏈、不同穩定幣、不同流動性池裡的美元重新整合，並在兌換、跨鏈和結算過程中持續降低滑價、Gas 波動和路徑成本，誰就握住了離使用者最近、也最難被繞開的入口。
順著這個判斷，Bitget Wallet 正在探索「美元帳戶（dollar account）」的產品方向：讓使用者在一個自我託管帳戶裡，跨鏈、跨幣種地持有和使用美元，而不必操心手裡的美元到底是哪一種穩定幣。
作為 Open Standard 的成員之一，Bitget Wallet 研究院觀察這場變革，真正關心的並不是 OUSD 會不會成為下一種主流穩定幣，而是一個更長期的問題：當發行方的名字越來越不重要，誰會成為使用者進入鏈上美元世界的預設帳戶？
結語
過去十年，穩定幣的核心故事是：誰能合法、可信地把美元搬上鏈。
而當 140 家公司願意圍繞同一套標準，重新分配穩定幣最誘人的儲備收益，這個故事就開始翻頁了。發行數位美元本身，不再是一門可以獨佔利潤的生意，而更像一張入場券：它讓玩家進入下一代金融清算網路，但真正的價值不一定留在發行方手裡。
新的戰爭，發生在美元如何流動、如何結算、如何被使用者使用的那一層。誰定義標準，誰掌握清算路徑，誰能把散落在不同鏈、不同穩定幣、不同流動性池裡的美元，重新聚合成使用者眼裡的「一個美元」，誰就更接近下一代金融入口。
當發行美元不再足夠賺錢，美元的權力究竟屬於誰？是印出它的人，是讓它流動的那張網路，還是那個把碎片化美元重新拼回「一個美元」的帳戶？
這個答案，可能不再寫在任何一家發行方的資產負債表上，而會寫在網路裡，寫在帳戶裡，也寫在使用者每一次預設選擇裡。
常見問題
什麼是 Open USD（OUSD）？
Open USD 是 2026 年 6 月由 Open Standard 聯合 Visa、萬事達卡、貝萊德、Stripe、Coinbase 等 140 多家公司推出的新美元穩定幣，特色是鑄造贖回零手續費、無額度上限，儲備利息扣掉管理費後幾乎全數返還給分發合作方。
Open USD 會取代 USDC、USDT 嗎？
短期不會。文章指出穩定幣真正的護城河在流動性與使用慣性，PYUSD、USDG 等聯盟型穩定幣營運數年市值仍只有數十億美元，與上千億的 USDT、USDC 差一到兩個數量級。OUSD 帶來的更像「重新定價」而非「替代」。

〈台灣自動駕駛何時開放？特斯FSD審查估計最快年底才有結果〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
財團法人車輛安全審驗中心（車安中心）於 7 月 9 日發布公告，說明台灣特斯拉申請 FSD（Supervised）的審查辦理情形：案件目前處於「道路測試計畫審查」階段，中心近期將召開技術審議會議，優先檢視測試計畫能否驗證台灣特有的交通場景。綜合先前立法院討論會揭露的時程推算，若各階段順利銜接，FSD 最快有機會在 2026 年底完成審驗、開放台灣車主使用。
（前情提要：特斯拉FSD台灣正式送件！6/30停售買斷制，訂閱月費估3千元，審查進入技術委員會階段）
（背景補充：台灣等不到Tesla自動駕駛FSD？一場立法院討論會把現狀攤開來說）
一則掛在車安中心官網的行政公告，點閱數在短短幾天內突破一萬次。對於這個平日只發布法規說明、審驗制度文件的財團法人而言，這是極不尋常的數字——車安中心鮮少針對「單一車廠的送件案」對外發布公告，這次卻罕見地為台灣特斯拉的 FSD（Full Self-Driving，Supervised）申請案專門說明辦理情形，側面印證了國人對自動駕駛開放時程的高度關注。
罕見公告說了什麼？現在走到第一關
車安中心在 7 月 9 日的公告中證實，已受理台灣特斯拉依「申請新技術駕駛系統審查報告補充作業規定」提出的申請，業者須提交「國內道路環境適用性宣告及相關安全驗證測試報告」。整個審查程序分為四個階段：第一階段由業者提交道路測試計畫（目前案件所在位置）；第二階段是審查完成後報請交通部核定，業者據此展開道路測試；第三階段為業者完成測試後，提交安全驗證報告供審查；最後審查核定通過，才核發型式安全審驗合格證。
換言之，特斯拉 6 月 16 日正式遞件後，案件已進入四階段中的第一關。車安中心在公告中強調，將召開「技術審議會議」，優先檢視測試計畫是否能驗證「我國特有交通場景」等在地化情境，並審查功能安全、道路適用性及法規對應。對照台灣都會區高密度的機車混合車流、狹窄巷弄與特有的路口號誌設計，這正是 FSD 在歐美累積的驗證數據無法直接移植的部分。
車安中心表示，將以「嚴謹、客觀、科學」的態度辦理審查，在兼顧產業創新與用路人安全的前提下審慎推進；審查期程視業者測試進度與會議辦理情形而定。
審查通常要多久？前兩關約一個半月
車安中心沒有在公告中承諾時間表，但審查的「標準節奏」其實在送件前就已被攤開。根據立委葛如鈞 6 月 10 日邀集交通部公共運輸及監理司、車安中心召開的「推進自駕科技在台落地與 FSD 審驗流程討論會」會議紀錄，廠商正式送件後，車安中心原則上會在 2 至 4 週內召開首次技術審議會議，審查申請文件與道路測試計畫；初審可行後報請交通部核定，報部流程約 2 週內完成，隨即啟動道路測試。也就是說，從送件到「獲准上路測試」，制度上的標準期程約一個月至一個半月。
值得注意的是，這套審查不需要修法。交通部在同場會議中說明，FSD（Supervised）屬於 SAE Level 2 駕駛輔助技術，駕駛人仍須全程監控並負完全責任，因此可直接透過現行行政辦法進行事前審驗與道路測試，只有涉及責任轉移的 Level 3 以上才有修法需求。此外，交通部已採認荷蘭 RDW 對特斯拉 FSD 的國家級認證結果作為技術可行性的參考基礎，無須等待歐盟的最終投票排程，這讓文件審查階段少了一大塊重複驗證的工作；交通部也早在 5 月 27 日邀集高公局、公路局預先協調國道與快速道路的測試配套，避免送件後才從零開始。
真正的變數在道路測試本身。車安中心已言明審查期程「視業者測試進度」而定——測試要開多久、跑多少里程、涵蓋哪些場景，取決於技術審議會議核定的測試計畫內容，這也是目前整條時間軸上彈性最大的一段。
技術審議會議會找哪些專家？
車安中心公告僅表示將邀集「相關機關與專家」召開技術審議會議，未公布名單。不過從審查標的（功能安全、道路適用性、法規對應、在地化場景驗證）與國內車輛審驗慣例來看，顧問與審議專家預料將涵蓋以下領域：
- 車輛工程與功能安全: 熟悉 ISO 26262（功能安全）與 SOTIF（預期功能安全）的學者與驗證機構代表，負責檢視系統失效時的安全機制
- 交通工程與道路安全: 評估測試計畫是否涵蓋台灣特有場景——機車混流、路邊臨停、公車專用道與複雜路口，這是公告點名的優先審查項目
- 人工智慧與感知系統: 檢視純視覺方案在台灣道路標線、號誌與天候條件下的辨識可靠度
- 資通安全: 對應 UN R155/R156 車輛網路安全與軟體更新（OTA）規範，FSD 功能正是透過 OTA 推送
- 人因工程與監理法制: 評估駕駛監控機制（DMS）能否確保駕駛人維持注意力，以及肇事責任、保險與罰則的法規對應
主管機關端則預料由交通部公共運輸及監理司、公路局、高速公路局等單位與會，分別對應法規解釋與測試路段的管理權責。
各階段要多久？最快年底、保守明年上半年
綜合公告揭示的四階段程序、立法院討論會確立的標準期程，以及道路測試的合理區間，各階段時程可以這樣推演：
- 技術審議會議（7 月中下旬）: 特斯拉 6 月 16 日送件，依 2 至 4 週慣例，首次會議應於 7 月內召開；車安中心公告也證實「近期將辦理」
- 測試計畫報部核定（8 月上旬）: 初審通過後報請交通部核定約需 2 週，若計畫需補件修正則順延
- 道路測試（約 8 月至 11 月）: 估計需 3 個月上下，須在國道、快速道路與市區道路累積足夠的在地化驗證數據；此為全程彈性最大的階段
- 安全驗證報告審查與核發合格證（約 1 至 2 個月）: 測試報告送回技術審議會議審查，通過後報部核定、核發型式安全審驗合格證
把四段時程接起來：如果測試計畫一次過關、道路測試順利，FSD 最快可望在 2026 年 12 月完成審驗，隨後透過 OTA 推送給台灣車主；只要任何一關需要補件、擴大測試範圍，時間就會往 2027 年上半年遞延。特斯拉在 7 月 1 日起停售 FSD 一次性買斷方案、轉向訂閱制的動作，也被市場解讀為替開放後的商業模式預作準備。
對消費者而言，比「何時開放」更值得留意的是開放的形式：FSD（Supervised）是 Level 2 駕駛輔助，不是自動駕駛——駕駛人雙手可暫離方向盤，但法律責任一分未減。車安中心這份罕見的公告，與其說是進度報告，不如說是在破萬點閱的關注度下，先替社會大眾把「審查會怎麼走」說清楚。下一個關鍵節點，就看 7 月的首次技術審議會議放不放行測試計畫。

title: 貝格先生分析》BTC 長期、短期持有者成本逆轉訊號，數據上怎麼推算
summary:
加密分析師貝格先生（@market_beggar）在動區「學院計畫」專欄分享一項熊市底部訊號：當比特幣「短期持 […]

〈貝格先生分析》BTC 長期、短期持有者成本逆轉訊號，數據上怎麼推算〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
加密分析師貝格先生（@market_beggar）在動區「學院計畫」專欄分享一項熊市底部訊號：當比特幣「短期持有者平均成本（STH-RP）」跌破「長期持有者平均成本（LTH-RP）」時，歷史上無一例外對應到熊市底部區域。他根據現有資料推演，兩者正以每日約 199 美元的速度接近，估計約 106 天後可能再次觸發此訊號。本文為 貝格先生 的研究文章，與動區合作專欄。
（前情提要：貝格先生分析》市場的寒武紀階段：第二項週期性底部訊號出現）
（背景補充：貝格先生分析》BTC「史詩級底部共振」再現！偏離度調整的 STH-RP 模型新資料分享）
重點摘要
- 貝格先生指 STH-RP（短期持有者成本）跌破 LTH-RP（長期持有者成本）時，歷史上無一例外對應 BTC 熊市底部
- 目前 STH-RP 為 70,558 美元、LTH-RP 為 49,495 美元，兩者差距 21,063 美元
- 兩者以每日約 199 美元速度接近，推估約 106 天後可能再次觸發底部訊號
談及深熊的抄底策略，除了我平時最常分享的「四大深熊模型」，其實還有一項同樣也非常值得注意的訊號，也就是「短期持有者成本，短暫低於長期持有者成本」。
本文，我將特別針對此話題，根據現有的資料，帶各位進行一次簡易的資料推演。
圖：STH-RP（藍）與 LTH-RP（綠）歷史走勢，每次 STH-RP 跌破 LTH-RP 都對應到熊市底部區域 | 資料來源：貝格先生（@market_beggar）
附圖的指標概念如下：
🔺 藍線（🟦）= STH-RP（短期持有者平均成本）
🔺 綠線（🟩）= LTH-RP（長期持有者平均成本）
🔺 訊號 = STH-RP < LTH-RP
貝格的老朋友都知道：
➡️ 因短期持有者交易頻繁，顧 STH-RP 對於價格的變化更敏感
➡️ 長期持有者則更像是「聰明錢」，具有明顯的成本優勢
在大部分時間內，按理而言 LTH-RP 應低於 STH-RP；如果出現了「STH-RP < LTH-RP」的怪狀，說明市場價格不僅已經跌破了長期持有者的持倉成本，並且還在 LTH-RP 之下停留了一段時間，才可能使 STH-RP 逐步降低，最終低於 LTH-RP。
沒錯，市況若要如此慘澹，基本只可能發生在熊市底部。
如附圖所示：自 BTC 誕生至今，每次訊號出現（STH-RP < LTH-RP）時，無一例外的都對應到 BTC 的熊市底部區域。
時間回到現在，根據現有的資料，我們可以得出以下推演：
➡️ 目前 STH-RP = 70,558
➡️ 目前 LTH-RP = 49,495
➡️ 兩者差距 = 70,558 – 49,495 = 21,063
再來，如果我們從去年 10 月初開始計算：
➡️ 去年 10/01 至今，一共經過了 273 日
➡️ STH-RP 自 112,233 開始下降，平均降速 = 153 元 / 日
➡️ LTH-RP 自 36,825 開始上升，平均升速 = 46 元 / 日
最後，我們便可得出以下結論：
➡️ 兩者以平均每日 (153+46) = 199 元 / 日的速度接近
➡️ 兩者在 21,063 / 199 = 106 日後，就可能再次觸發訊號💡
當然，以上資料只是粗糙的概算，實際情況不可能如此簡單，但至少上述結論可以稍微提供一些研究的方向。
但不論如何，不可否認的是：我們的確已經位於熊市的後期階段，屬於多軍的黎明真的不遠了。
常見問題
什麼是 STH-RP 和 LTH-RP？
STH-RP（短期持有者平均成本）指近期買入者的平均持倉成本，對價格變化較敏感；LTH-RP（長期持有者平均成本）則是長期持有者的平均成本，被視為「聰明錢」。當 STH-RP 跌破 LTH-RP，通常代表市場已處於熊市底部區域。
這個熊市底部訊號現在觸發了嗎？
尚未。貝格先生指出目前 STH-RP 約 70,558 美元，仍高於 LTH-RP 的 49,495 美元，兩者差距 21,063 美元。依每日約 199 美元的接近速度概算，約 106 天後才可能再次觸發，且屬粗略推估。

title: Stripe 幹大事！拉私募 Advent 砸 530 億鎂併購 PayPal，每股喊 60.5 鎂
summary:
支付新星 Stripe 出手了！路透社獨家報導 Stripe 聯手私募巨頭 Advent Internatio […]

〈Stripe 幹大事！拉私募 Advent 砸 530 億鎂併購 PayPal，每股喊 60.5 鎂〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
支付新星 Stripe 出手了！路透社獨家報導 Stripe 聯手私募巨頭 Advent International，以每股 60.50 美元、總估值超過 530 億美元的價碼，聯合出價收購昔日支付霸主 PayPal 溢價約 28%，背後還有約 500 億美元的銀行融資撐腰。今年 2 月才傳過的收購風聲，這次變成白紙黑字的正式報價；PayPal 尚未回應，但股價盤前一度飆漲近 15%。
（前情提要：經濟時報：PayPal 未與 Stripe 展開收購談判「結構性挑戰猶存」，PYPL 股價漲勢急剎）
（背景補充：幣圈史上最大收購案！支付巨頭 Stripe 豪砸 11 億鎂買下穩定幣平台 Bridge）
重點摘要
- 路透 7/15 獨家，Stripe 聯手私募 Advent International 出價每股 60.50 美元收購 PayPal，估值逾 530 億美元
- 報價較 PayPal 週二收盤溢價約 28%，背後有約 500 億美元銀行融資，兩家各持一半股權
- PayPal 過去一年市值蒸發逾 40%、一度低至約 360 億美元，訊息傳出股價盤前飆漲近 15%
路透社 7 月 15 日獨家報導，支付新創龍頭 Stripe 拉上私募股權巨頭 Advent International，向昔日支付霸主 PayPal 遞出一份聯合收購提案，開價每股 60.50 美元，把 PayPal 整體估值抬到超過 530 億美元，較 PayPal 週二收盤價溢價約 28%。這筆交易背後，還有約 500 億美元的銀行承諾融資撐腰。
一家自己都還沒上市的支付新星，聯手私募基金去吞下老字號的上市巨頭，光是這個組合就夠讓華爾街坐直身子。根據提案，Stripe 跟 Advent 打算各持一半股權、聯合擁有 PayPal，而且暫時不打算把 PayPal 的業務拆開來賣。這場接觸其實從 4 月初就開始，7 月稍早才正式遞出報價，目前 PayPal 還沒給出回應，買方希望未來幾週把談判往前推。當然，這種量級的交易能不能真的成交，變數還很大。
昔日霸主怎麼淪落到被收購？
被盯上的 PayPal，這幾年日子並不好過。成長放緩、數位支付賽道殺成紅海，PayPal 過去 12 個月市值蒸發超過 40%，2026 年一度低到只剩約 360 億美元。換句話說，這份 530 億美元的報價，對股東來說是一個難以忽視的溢價數字，也難怪訊息一齣，PayPal 股價盤前一度飆漲近 15%。
其實這也不是第一次傳出風聲。今年 2 月市場就傳過 Stripe 有意收購 PayPal，當時 PayPal 出面澄清「未展開談判」、還點出雙方「結構性挑戰猶存」，PYPL 的漲勢當場急剎。半年過去，傳聞這回變成了白紙黑字的正式報價。以下是這份提案的關鍵條件：
- 買方: Stripe 與私募 Advent International 聯合出價，交易後各持一半股權
- 報價: 每股 60.50 美元，總估值逾 530 億美元，溢價約 28%
- 融資: 約 500 億美元銀行承諾融資撐腰
- 進度: 4 月初初步接洽、7 月正式報價，PayPal 尚未回應
這場併購底層是一場穩定幣戰爭
對動區讀者來說，這筆交易真正的看點在穩定幣。Stripe 這兩年火力全開布局加密支付，2024 年豪砸 11 億美元吃下穩定幣基建 Bridge，2025 年又收購加密錢包商 Privy，還自研了 Tempo 鏈。PayPal 這邊則手握自家穩定幣 PYUSD，已經擴充套件到全球 70 國，還跟 Stablechain 等專用鏈繫結。
一邊是埋頭自己蓋穩定幣帝國的 Stripe，一邊是坐擁 PYUSD 現成使用者基礎的 PayPal，如果併購真的談成，等於把兩套穩定幣布局裝進同一個口袋，對整個支付與穩定幣戰局的意義，遠遠不只是換個老闆這麼簡單。
常見問題
Stripe 真的要收購 PayPal 嗎？
據路透報導，Stripe 已聯手私募 Advent International 向 PayPal 遞出每股 60.50 美元、估值逾 530 億美元的聯合收購提案，溢價約 28%。但 PayPal 尚未回應，交易仍在早期階段，不保證最終成交。
Stripe 收購 PayPal 跟穩定幣有什麼關係？
兩家公司都重押穩定幣。Stripe 2024 年砸 11 億美元收購穩定幣基建 Bridge、自研 Tempo 鏈；PayPal 則有自家穩定幣 PYUSD，已擴充套件至全球 70 國。併購若成，等於整合兩套穩定幣布局。

title: 破解虛擬資產「二次詐騙」！幣託攜手刑事局、水豐刀公私協力傳授防禦心法
summary:
臺灣金融科技協會（TFTA）六月舉辦「虛擬資產詐騙手法破解」線上論壇，由幣託集團（BitoGroup）創辦人暨 […]

〈破解虛擬資產「二次詐騙」！幣託攜手刑事局、水豐刀公私協力傳授防禦心法〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
臺灣金融科技協會（TFTA）六月舉辦「虛擬資產詐騙手法破解」線上論壇，由幣託集團（BitoGroup）創辦人暨執行長鄭光泰主持，聯手刑事局偵查隊長洪丞奇與區塊鏈 YouTuber 水豐刀，從交易所、執法機關與民間教育三大視角，拆解「二次詐騙」等新型態科技詐騙手法並傳授防禦心法。
（前情提要：臺灣虛擬通貨公會正式成立：幣託鄭光泰出任理事長、XREX 蕭滙宗副理事長）
（背景補充：完整解讀臺灣加密貨幣專法《虛擬資產服務法》：交易所走入牌照制）
重點摘要
＊本文為 幣託集團（BitoGroup） 提供之新聞稿。
臺灣金融科技協會（TFTA）於六月舉辦「金融資安與反詐騙，虛擬資產詐騙手法破解」線上論壇，由幣託集團（BitoGroup）創辦人暨執行長鄭光泰主持，聯手刑事局偵查隊長洪丞奇與知名區塊鏈 YouTuber 水豐刀，從交易所、執法機關與民間教育三大視角深度拆解新型態科技詐騙，攜手築起最強金融防線。
水豐刀拆解「二次詐騙」陷阱
水豐刀指出，虛擬資產詐騙的終極形態就是「二次詐騙」。不法集團的操作通常分為四個階段：首先，在受害者初期給予小額獲利後，慫恿投入大筆資金以獲取高額報酬；中後期拒絕出金，並編造補稅、保證金等各種藉口要求加碼，再誘導受害者將資金移往真假難辨的惡意 App 或網站；最後則是孤立受害者，阻止其向家人、外界求援，進而假冒律師或駭客宣稱能追回款項，誘使受害者落入二次詐騙的深淵。
幣託鄭光泰：交易所部署科技防線
幣託創辦人暨執行長鄭光泰說明，不法份子常利用資訊落差進行複合型詐騙。幣託身為合規交易平台，已投入巨大成本部署科技聯防，包含匯入國際級 KYC 模組以有效辨識與監控客戶身分，落實反洗錢（AML）與防制資恐（CFT）要求；同時部署可疑交易監控系統主動偵測異常行為，並由客服團隊針對高風險使用者進行電話關懷。
在跨域聯防方面，交易所已串接檢調與銀行通報系統以共享可疑金流情資，並全力配合法務單位處置異常帳號。鄭光泰提醒，民眾可善用平台提供的安全機制，如通行金鑰 Passkey、二階段驗證器（2FA）等，自主提升帳號安全防護。
刑事局洪丞奇：「引蛇出洞」反擊法則
刑事局詐欺犯罪防制中心偵查隊長洪丞奇解析，虛擬貨幣詐騙中高達七成以上屬於「假交友結合投資」。詐騙集團常花費數月寒暄建立信任，再手把手引導受害者至國內合規交易所買入 USDT 穩定幣並轉入不法錢包。洪丞奇打破大眾迷思指出，許多被害人的資產消失並非錢包被駭，而是受害者缺乏資安觀念，不小心將私鑰或助記詞截圖外流，或盲目點選惡意智慧合約授權，形同「雙手奉上保險箱鑰匙」。
針對防範與反擊策略，洪丞奇建議民眾可至內政部警政署「打詐儀錶板」查詢最新詐騙案例；若遇到可疑的錢包地址，也可善用鏈上工具核對該地址是否已被標記為高風險。若發現受騙，千萬不要立刻攤牌，以免被詐騙集團封鎖並銷毀證據，建議維持日常人設並佯稱資金被鎖定，利用對方貪婪心理主動提議面交現金，藉此配合檢警布局面交、引蛇出洞。
公私協力全面聯防，共同守護數位資產
鄭光泰強調，打擊虛擬資產犯罪不能單打獨鬥，唯有透過交易所、執法機關、民間教育的公私協力，輔以民眾建立識詐與防禦觀念，才能打造真正安心的數位資產環境。身兼虛擬資產公會理事長的鄭光泰預告，國內業者將匯入國際規範 Travel Rule（旅行規則），透過蒐集並驗證傳送方與接收方資訊以強化交易監控，有效防制洗錢及資恐風險，進一步提升金融體系的透明度。
常見問題
什麼是虛擬資產「二次詐騙」？
二次詐騙是詐騙集團在受害者受騙後，假冒律師或駭客宣稱能追回被騙款項，誘使受害者再次落入陷阱。水豐刀指出這是虛擬資產詐騙的終極形態，也是四階段操作的最後一步。
發現被虛擬資產詐騙後該怎麼辦？
刑事局洪丞奇建議，發現受騙後千萬不要立刻攤牌，以免詐騙集團封鎖並銷毀證據。可維持日常人設佯稱資金被鎖定，利用對方貪婪心理提議面交現金，配合檢警布局「引蛇出洞」。
關於幣託集團（BitoGroup）
幣託集團（BitoGroup）成立於 2014 年，致力於用最簡單的方式讓區塊鏈進入每個人的日常生活，並協助企業與消費者進入 Web3 時代。幣託運用區塊鏈和高頻交易技術，積極打造創新的企業級虛擬資產核心品牌「Bito.Enterprise」，包括穩定幣結算、點數換加密貨幣及加密貨幣支付。BitoPro 加密貨幣交易所已完成金管會「提供虛擬資產服務之事業或人員洗錢防制登記」，提供加密貨幣錢包和交易服務，亦支援法幣出入金、超商購買或點數換加密貨幣。官方網站：https://www.bitopro.com

title: 重磅！日本參議院拍板：加密資產屬於金融商品！稅率砍到 20%、替比特幣 ETF 鋪路
summary:
日本參議院財政金融委員會 7 月 14 日以多數贊成透過《金融商品取引法》與《資金決済法》等修正案，本會議預計 […]

〈重磅！日本參議院拍板：加密資產屬於金融商品！稅率砍到 20%、替比特幣 ETF 鋪路〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
日本參議院財政金融委員會 7 月 14 日以多數贊成透過《金融商品取引法》與《資金決済法》等修正案，本會議預計 7 月 15 日拍板成立，把加密資產從「支付手段」正式改列「金融商品」。無牌販售的刑責從 3 年以下拉高到 10 年以下，並首度把內線交易納管；稅制方面則從最高 55% 的綜合課稅，改為約 20% 的分離課稅。
（前情提要：日本脩金融法升格加密貨幣為金融商品，內線交易入罪、2028 年 ETF 上路）
（背景補充：日本擬引入加密貨幣「分離課稅制度」：稅率統一為 20%）
重點摘要
- 日本參議院 7 月 15 日表決透過金商法與資金決済法修正案，加密資產從「支付手段」正式改列「金融商品」。
- 無牌販售刑責從 3 年以下拉高到 10 年以下、罰金上限從 300 萬日圓提高到 1000 萬日圓，並首度納管內線交易。
- 稅制從最高 55% 綜合課稅改為約 20% 分離課稅、虧損可 3 年結轉，預計 2028 年上路，同時替現貨比特幣 ETF 開路。
日本國會為加密資產監管翻開全新一頁。據 日本經濟新聞 報導，日本參議院財政金融委員會在 7 月 14 日以多數贊成，透過《金融商品取引法》與《資金決済法》等一系列修正案，本會議預計 7 月 15 日正式表決成立，最快趕在 7 月 17 日會期結束前完成立法。眾議院早在 6 月 11 日就已透過，參議院這一關過了，法案等於正式落地。
過去日本把加密資產放在《資金決済法》底下，當成一種「支付手段」來管；修法之後，它被移到規範股票、債券的《金融商品取引法》，正式成為「金融商品」。定性一變，整套投資人保護與不公平交易的框架就跟著套上來。
無牌重罰，內線交易入罪
先是罰得更重。針對沒有登記就販售加密資產的業者，拘禁刑上限從 3 年以下一口氣拉到 10 年以下，罰金上限也從 300 萬日圓提高到 1000 萬日圓。
發行方、交易所營運商，以及任何掌握上架、下架、重大技術事故等未公開重要資訊的人，都不準搶在訊息公開前交易。這代表交易所自己人先知道要上下架哪個幣、然後偷跑進場的空間，被正式堵上。
修正案還要求 IEO（首次交易所發行）須公開基本資訊，並為個人投資人設定投資上限，特定加密資產發行者也得定期履行資訊公開義務，向散戶靠攏一大步。
稅率從 55% 砍到 20%
對散戶最有感的是稅。現行制度下，加密資產的獲利被歸為「雜項所得」，跟著綜合所得一起累進課稅，最高稅率可以逼近 55%。修法後改採「申告分離課稅」，稅率壓到約 20%（含地方稅約 20.315%），而且比照股票，虧損可以在 3 年內結轉扣抵。
這一刀砍下去，等於把加密資產跟股票放到同一張稅表上。不過稅制不會馬上生效，預計要到 2028 年才上路，金商法相關規定則在 2027 年度先行實施。
替比特幣 ETF 鋪路
把加密資產納入《金融商品取引法》，還開啟了另一扇門，那就是現貨加密 ETF。一旦加密資產成為法律認可的金融商品，發行掛牌現貨 ETF 的法律障礙就被清掉，東京證券交易所已經表態，最快 2027 年就能開始交易。
日本財務大臣片山皋月上週才鬆口，直言加密 ETF 該解禁、日本不能再缺席。從 2024 年底金融廳丟擲構想，到眾議院、參議院陸續點頭，日本花了大半年把這套改革推到終點線。接下來就看 2027、2028 兩個時間點，制度真正落地時能不能兌現這波政策紅利。
常見問題
日本把加密資產改列金融商品有什麼影響？
加密資產監管從《資金決済法》移到《金融商品取引法》，適用與股票、債券相同的投資人保護與不公平交易規範，包括首度納管的內線交易，發行方與交易所掌握未公開資訊時禁止搶先交易。
日本加密資產稅率何時從 55% 降到 20%？
修正案將加密資產所得從最高約 55% 的綜合課稅，改為約 20% 的申告分離課稅，虧損可在 3 年內結轉扣抵，預計 2028 年實施，金商法相關規定則於 2027 年度先行上路。

日本財務大臣片山皋月鬆口：加密ETF該解禁了，日本不能再缺席

title: 外送專法等了6年！下週正式上路，每趟最低報酬45元，爭議在哪？
summary:
台灣將推出外送專法《外送員權益保障及外送平台管理法》將於 2026 年 7 月 21 日正式上路。這部法把每筆 […]

〈外送專法等了6年！下週正式上路，每趟最低報酬45元，爭議在哪？〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
台灣將推出外送專法《外送員權益保障及外送平台管理法》將於 2026 年 7 月 21 日正式上路。這部法把每筆訂單最低報酬 45 元、疊單必須逐筆計價、演算法派單要透明、平台強制投保等規定全都寫進法律，替全台約 15 萬名外送員撐起安全網。但它繞過了爭論最久的那個問題，外送員到底是「承攬」還是「僱傭」，也因此在上路前夕，勞團、平台與消費者三方仍在拉扯。
（前情提要：Grab 宣布六億美元併購台灣 foodpanda，Web3 錢包、加密支付能否跟著進場？）
（背景補充：美國外送平台 DoorDash 聯手支付公鏈 Tempo，探索使用穩定幣發薪與結算）
重點摘要
- 台灣首部外送專法 2026 年 1 月 6 日三讀、7 月 21 日施行，涵蓋約 15 萬名外送員
- 每筆訂單最低報酬 45 元、疊單逐筆計價、平台強制投保團體傷害險與職災險，並隨最低工資調整
- 專法保留承攬與僱傭的彈性，未強制認定僱傭，勞團憂心「承攬身份被就地合法」
我們開頭就要回憶兩件外送造成的死亡車禍，2019 年 10 月國慶連假，台灣有兩個外送員再也沒有回家。
10 月 10 日深夜，桃園一名 29 歲的馬姓 foodpanda 外送員與小貨車對撞，飛摔身亡。那天是他開始跑外送第二天。
三天後，10 月 13 日，士林街頭一名 20 歲出頭的黃姓 Uber Eats 外送員在收工途中遭汽車追撞，送醫不治。
兩條人命，只隔了三天。
連假過完的星期一，勞動部火速出面認定這兩起個案屬於「僱傭」關係，外送員應該享有勞工該有的保障，並隨即發動勞檢、對兩家平台開罰。平台也很快回應，說會負擔個案的後續賠償與協助。但兩家都重申同一句話：旗下外送員是「承攬」夥伴，不是「僱傭」員工。
這個爭議第一次被整個社會看見，在意的人可能只有外送員族群。六年後的 2026 年 7 月 21 日，台灣首部外送專法終於要上路。中間隔著六年和不只兩條人命。
「承攬」
要理解這部法為什麼重要，得先搞懂「承攬」和「僱傭」差在哪。這兩個詞聽起來像法律課本裡的名詞，但對每天騎車上路的人來說，它是實實在在的保護，有或沒有的差別。
如果是「僱傭」，你就是勞工，受《勞動基準法》保障。僱主要幫你保勞保、負擔大部分保費，你有勞退帳戶、有職災的法定給付，出了事有一整套制度接住你。如果是「承攬」，你在法律上比較像一個自己接案的小老闆，這些通通得自己來。勞保得自己透過工會加保、自己扛大半保費，沒有勞退，職災則要看平台有沒有買商業保險，而商業保險是可能拒賠的。
過去十幾年，外送平台幾乎都把外送員歸類成「承攬合作夥伴」。foodpanda 的合約甚至白紙黑字，要外送員同意「不對公司提起因提供服務而生的任何僱傭相關請求」，等於先一步堵住你日後主張自己是員工的路。
問題是外送員的處境卡在一個很尷尬的灰色地帶。說他是承攬，他確實可以自由上線、自由拒單，像個接案者；可說他是僱傭，他的每一筆報酬怎麼算、能不能被優先派單、什麼情況會被停權，又全都握在平台的演算法手裡。他有接案者的自由，卻沒有接案者的議價權。
這正是外送員長年真正的困境，出事的時候，沒有人要負全責。
45 元外送一趟的「底薪」
新上路的專法做的第一件事，就是替這份工作畫出幾條過去從來沒有的底線。
最受關注的是報酬，專法規定，每一筆訂單的基本報酬不得低於外送服務期間依比例換算最低工資時薪的 1.25 倍，而且設有每單至少 45 元的保障金額，未來還會跟著最低工資一起調整。報酬必須全額直接給付、每月至少發兩次，並且要提供可以核對的明細。
再來是大家常忽略的「疊單」，過去平台可以一次派好幾單給同一個外送員，卻用併單的方式壓低單價。新法規定，每筆訂單就是一個取件點、一個送達點，就算同時派送多單，也必須逐筆計算報酬，不能再靠併單稀釋掉外送員的收入。
再來是在平台背後運作的演算法，專法要求平台把派單、計酬的機制攤開來，資訊要透明。更重要的是停權，過去外送員常常在毫無預警下就被「關帳號」，斷了生計卻求助無門。新法規定，平台要停權必須說明理由、負舉證責任，還要提供申訴機會，並設立一個包含工會代表的獨立處理小組。
安全的部分，平台必須替外送員投保團體傷害險與責任險，沒保完就不準派單上線，並且要負擔外送員參加勞工職業災害保險的保費。六年前那兩起事故裡的法律真空，總算有了法律去填。
把這些放在一起看，這部法照顧的其實不只外送員。它同時規範了平台的管理責任、保障了商家不被任意調整拆帳、也讓消費者知道自己付的錢有沒有流到該去的地方。這是台灣第一次用中央層級的專法，把外送員、平台、商家、消費者一起放進同個規則。
為什麼還是有人不滿意
照理說屬於特定領域勞工的法規，上路之時應該收到支持。但在上路前夕，幾乎每一方都有不滿。
最深的不爽還是回到「承攬」兩個字。這部專法選擇的路線，是不強制認定外送員到底是承攬還是僱傭，而是不論契約形式，平台都必須負起最低保障責任。勞動部長洪申翰的說法是，新型態的平台未來也可能會用僱傭的方式聘外送員，法律應該保留彈性，容納不同的關係。
這個折衷有它的務實道理，卻也讓不少勞團憂心，當保障可以在承攬的框架裡給，平台是不是就更沒有動機把外送員轉成正式員工？換句話說這部法可能把「承攬」勞工身份就地合法化，讓外送員拿到了安全網，卻也被更牢地留在勞基法的門外。退休金、資遣費、完整的勞工身份，仍然吃不到。
另一個吵得很兇的是錢。專法通過後，運費會不會漲，就成了消費者最直接的焦慮。消基會直言，平台很可能把保障外送員所增加的成本，轉嫁到消費者身上。
Uber 則引用公平會的研究示警，如果運費漲個 5%，可能會有三成四的民眾乾脆不叫外送，反而讓部分外送員失去接單機會。平台業者也不諱言法遵成本上升，運費調漲「勢在必行」。
更微妙的是，專法上路前後，市場已經傳出平台打算把運費調高三成、甚至想向外送員收取「媒合費」的風聲，讓工會直批「吃相難看」，認為這是把成本硬塞回最沒有議價能力的那一方。要保障外送員的法規，會不會反而變成漲價和轉嫁成本的理由，成了它上路後最現實的考驗。
你上一次叫外送運費多少錢？7 月 21 日之後，那個數字可能會不太一樣。多出來的錢會落進誰的口袋？
外送環境要改變了
這六年之間，外送早就從新鮮的都市風景，變成幾百萬人生活裡理所當然的服務。送餐的人在雨裡、在車陣裡奔馳，在你家樓下按電鈴，從制度的邊緣走到制度裡面。
這部專法沒辦法一次解決所有事。它跨過了報酬、保險、演算法透明這幾道最急迫的關卡，卻在承攬與僱傭那道最根本的線前面，選擇先繞過去。它接住了很多過去接不住的人，但也留下了同樣清楚的空白。
常見問題
外送專法什麼時候上路？主要保障什麼？
《外送員權益保障及外送平台管理法》2026 年 1 月 6 日三讀透過、7 月 21 日正式施行。核心保障包括每單最低報酬 45 元、疊單逐筆計價、演算法派單透明、平台強制投保團體傷害險與職災險，以及停權須說明理由並提供申訴。
外送專法會讓外送變貴嗎？
可能會。平台指法遵與投保成本上升，運費調漲「勢在必行」，市場一度傳出運費上漲三成。消基會擔心成本轉嫁消費者，Uber 也引研究示警漲價恐讓部分民眾不再叫外送，實際影響要看 7 月 21 日上路後的市場反應。

title: WebX 2026》台灣加密專法通過背後：唐鳳、葛如鈞詳解數位治理下一步趨勢
summary:
台灣在 WebX 2026 展示虛擬資產 VASP 法與 AI 基本法等數位治理成果。唐鳳探討後發優勢，指出應以風險動態調整監管。

〈WebX 2026》台灣加密專法通過背後：唐鳳、葛如鈞詳解數位治理下一步趨勢〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
作者：Max，加密城市
唐鳳遠端登場，台灣專法成 WebX 焦點
WebX 2026 於 7 月 13 日在東京登場，台灣立法委員葛如鈞與台灣首任數位發展部部長、現任無任所大使唐鳳，在 CRYL 舞台進行特別對談，聚焦台灣 2026 年上半年接連完成的 2 項重要制度工程：虛擬資產服務提供者法（VASP 法）與 AI 基本法。唐鳳以遠端形式參與，從監管哲學、公民 AI 、去中心化身分，到 AI 代理人與區塊鏈結合，完整勾勒台灣數位治理下一階段方向。
葛如鈞是台灣 AI 基本法主要發起人之一，也是 VASP 法的重要共同發起人。他在對談中指出，台灣早在 2016 年就能於便利商店購買比特幣，但後續將近 10 年，加密產業始終處在監管灰色地帶。直到 2026 年，VASP 法於 6 月 13 日三讀通過，AI 基本法也在 1 月 14 日施行，台灣才正式從模糊架構走向明確制度。
從模糊走向明確，VASP 法補上監管缺口
唐鳳在對談中指出，「社會尚未形成共識」看似中立，實際上常讓已經有能力行動的一方取得優勢。
她認為，監管延宕會讓既得利益者繼續受益，台灣這次制度轉向的重點，是把原本由少數人掌握的解釋空間，改為透明、可討論、可執行的公共規則。
- VASP 法針對虛擬資產業者建立登錄制度，並納入客戶保護、反洗錢與營運管理要求。
- AI 基本法則以 20 條原則性規範，明確列出永續、人類自主、隱私、資安、透明、公平與問責 7 大原則。
兩部法律都未採取重罰優先路線，而是試圖在創新發展與權利保護之間建立制度邊界。對台灣而言，這代表加密資產與 AI 不再只靠行政指引或個案解釋運作，產業、投資人與開發者開始擁有更清楚的政策座標。
後發優勢成關鍵，監管要保留轉向能力
葛如鈞也提到，台灣在半導體制造上位居全球核心，但 AI 監管啟動時間晚於歐盟等地區。唐鳳回應，後發者的優勢在於能參考其它國家的制度經驗，並避免把快速變動的技術鎖進僵硬分類。她以「cybernetics」一詞的希臘語源說明，治理的核心並非一味追求加速，而是保有轉向能力。
唐鳳認為，好的 AI 監管不該只問今天的系統分類是否完美，因為大型模型已經進入能訓練小型模型的新階段，固定分級很快就會失準。她主張監管應以風險樣態調整，並讓各個社群依照自身需求吸收 AI 。
她也提到，日本以社群差異建立不同整合類型的作法，提供了亞洲政策設計的重要參考。換言之，AI 應進入人的治理迴圈，而非讓人被迫進入 AI 的操作邏輯。
公民 AI 與鏈上身分，成下一波治理基礎
對談後半段轉向公民 AI 與區塊鏈身分。唐鳳介紹她推動的「civic.ai」架構，強調資料不該被視為可從社群抽取、輸送到巨大雲端模型的石油，而應被視為能滋養社群知識的土壤。
她提出「Data is soil and never oil」的觀點，主張每個社群都可以擁有結合小型知識管理與 AI 的「commi」，讓 AI 成為跨黨派、跨文化溝通的橋梁。
隨著深偽與 AI 代理人普及，葛如鈞進一步提出身分驗證問題。唐鳳表示，人類本人的身分證明已可透過本地生物辨識與簽章技術大致解決，下一階段挑戰在於 AI 代理人的授權證明。若某個 AI 代理人代表個人進行交易或決策，系統必須能證明該代理人確實經本人授權。她也透露，自己的 commi「JTEAMI」已在以太坊上以 ERC-8004 、 Agent ID 22714 運作，並強調 AI 代理人若要代為交易，須通過可攜性、路徑可檢查性、社群部署治理與故障問責等測試。
唐鳳進一步指出，AI 代理人的可靠性可借鏡智能合約的形式化驗證方法。當程式碼規模龐大到無人能完整閱讀時，Lean 、 Dafny 等證明輔助工具可協助驗證不變條件，讓 AI 代理人的行為規則更可檢查。
葛如鈞則在結尾強調，科技政策需要透明與跨黨派合作。台灣從加密專法到 AI 基本法的推進，顯示數位治理已成為跨國、跨政黨的制度工程，也為日本與亞洲其它市場提供可觀察的政策案例。
（以上內容獲合作夥伴《加密城市》授權節錄及轉載，原文連結 ）

title: 斬斷伊朗金流！美財政部制裁 4 加密錢包、凍結 1.3 億美元 USDT
summary:
為了斬斷伊朗的地下金脈，美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）宣布，已將多個與伊朗相關的加密貨幣錢包列入制裁名單，導致超過 1.3 億美元的 USDT 遭凍結。

〈斬斷伊朗金流！美財政部制裁 4 加密錢包、凍結 1.3 億美元 USDT〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
為了斬斷伊朗的地下金脈，美國財政部長貝森特（Scott Bessent）宣布，已將多個與伊朗相關的加密貨幣錢包列入制裁名單，導致超過 1.3 億美元的 USDT 遭凍結。
這些遭制裁的錢包據信與伊朗央行有關聯，貝森特周二在社群平台 X 上表示：「我們將持續積極追查資金流向，阻止伊朗政權取得非法收益。」
.@USTreasury is committed to disrupting and degrading Iran’s illicit financial activities, including its abuse of digital assets. Today, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned multiple wallets tied to the Central Bank of Iran, resulting in the freeze of over $130…
— Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent (@SecScottBessent) July 14, 2026
儘管貝森特並未詳細說明除了列入制裁名單外，當局是否還採取了其他行動；但就在他發文的前幾分鐘，鏈上分析師 Specter 就披露，Tether 已在波場鏈（Tron）上凍結了 4 個錢包，這些錢包內合計持有高達 1.31 億美元的 USDT 。
Specter 指出，這些地址不僅與伊朗央行有關，更牽涉到伊朗伊斯蘭革命衛隊（IRGC）。他進一步補充，這筆龐大資金多數是從支付服務商 DTC Pay 以及加密貨幣交易所 Bitso 提領而出。不過在 Specter 發文當下，外界尚不清楚這些錢包遭凍結的確切原因，直到美國財政部隨後發表聲明，才證實了這波執法行動。
The wallet is linked OFAC sanctioned ISLAMIC REVOLUTIONARY GUARD CORPS (IRGC)- CENTRAL BANK OF THE ISLAMIC REPUBLIC OF IRAN (BANK MARKAZI JOMHOURI ISLAMI IRAN) pic.twitter.com/f0wlcHrYDR
— Specter (@SpecterAnalyst) July 14, 2026
事實上，這並非加密貨幣產業首度配合執法單位進行大規模封殺。近期已有一連串與 OFAC 制裁名單或執法調查相關的巨額 USDT 遭凍結；今年 4 月，在美國當局示警特定錢包涉嫌非法活動後，Tether 就協助凍結了 2 個 TRON 地址、總價值超過 3.44 億美元的 USDT 。
根據 Tether 公布的數據，截至今年 4 月為止，該公司已與全球 65 個國家的 340 多個執法單位建立合作，累計協助超過 2,300 起跨國調查案件；至今總計凍結超過 44 億美元的非法資產，其中超過 21 億美元皆是配合美國當局的掃蕩行動。

title: 韓國擬制定《國家資產基本法》，加密貨幣將納入管理
summary:
韓國政府今（15）日宣布，將制定全新的《國家資產基本法》，藉此推動政府資產管理系統現代化升級，並且把加密貨幣等新興資產納入國有資產管理制度，為數位資產建立更完整的法律框架。

〈韓國擬制定《國家資產基本法》，加密貨幣將納入管理〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
韓國政府今（15）日宣布，將制定全新的《國家資產基本法》，藉此推動政府資產管理系統現代化升級，並且把加密貨幣等新興資產納入國有資產管理制度，為數位資產建立更完整的法律框架。
韓國財政經濟部表示，現行的《國有財產法》制定於 1950 年，當時的立法思維完全是為了因應以「房地產」為核心的資產結構，時至今日，早已不敷現代複雜的金融環境所需。
韓國財政經濟部指出，新的法律框架將擴大「國有資產」的定義界線。未來，舉凡智慧財產權（IP）與虛擬資產都將納入管理範圍；同時，政府也將針對不同類別的資產，導入更專業的管理與運用機制。
韓國政府期盼，在這套新框架的運作下，國有資產管理將從過去偏重「保存、出售及基礎開發」的模式，轉向以提升資產價值為核心。
在周一召開的國務院會議上，韓國財政經濟部重申，儘管目前國家的科技戰略更聚焦於人工智慧（AI）發展，但對於推動區塊鏈、數位資產生態經濟發展的承諾依然堅定。
作為 2026 年下半年國家經濟成長戰略的重要一環，韓國也同步端出了區塊鏈產業的育成藍圖。未來的施政核心將包含 2 大重點：一、是持續推進央行數位貨幣（CBDC）的開發；二、則是加速完善《數位資產基本法》，建立專屬於加密貨幣、穩定幣的完整法律框架。

title: 槓上密西根州法院！美 CFTC 出手護航 Kalshi 、擋下「撤銷交易」命令
summary:
美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）與州政府之間圍繞預測市場的監管之爭持續升溫。CFTC 周二正式發布命令，禁止 Kalshi 按照密西根州法院要求，撤銷部分客戶已完成的交易，強調州法院無權要求受聯邦監管的交易平台違反《商品交易法》。

〈槓上密西根州法院！美 CFTC 出手護航 Kalshi 、擋下「撤銷交易」命令〉這篇文章最早發佈於《區塊客》。
full_text:
美國商品期貨交易委員會（CFTC）與州政府之間圍繞預測市場的監管之爭持續升溫。 CFTC 周二正式發布命令，禁止 Kalshi 按照密西根州法院要求，撤銷部分客戶已完成的交易，強調州法院無權要求受聯邦監管的交易平台違反《商品交易法》。
此舉也代表美國 CFTC 正式介入 Kalshi 與密西根州之間的法律衝突，進一步捍衛聯邦政府對預測市場的監管權。 CFTC 主席 Mike Selig 在聲明中表示：
委員會絕不容許州政府或州法院「脅迫」註冊實體違反《商品交易法》與 CFTC 的規範。
他強調，Kalshi 是經 CFTC 核准的指定合約市場（DCM），因此交易活動應完全受聯邦法規管轄。 Mike Selig 自上任以來，一直支持預測市場發展，也承諾建立更友善的監管環境，同時多次公開主張，CFTC 對預測市場擁有專屬管轄權，各州不得自行介入管理。
CFTC 與各州衝突持續擴大
近年來，美國已有多州政府主張，預測市場提供的事件合約（Event Contracts）本質上屬於非法賭博，因此要求 Kalshi 等平台停止營運，祭出禁令或裁罰。為此，CFTC 已陸續對多個州政府提起訴訟。
值得留意的是，密西根州是第一個試圖直接干預市場交易活動的州政府，Mike Selig 表示：
要求取消已成交的交易是前所未見的做法，不僅可能會對整個市場產生連鎖效應，也會破壞「契約確定性」，而這是維持市場正常運作的必要組成部分。
密西根法院要求取消交易，Kalshi 向 CFTC 緊急求助
事件起因於今年 6 月，密西根州一間巡迴法院應州檢察長要求，下令 Kalshi 停止在州內提供線上體育賽事預測合約。隨後，法院更要求 Kalshi 將部分密西根州用戶已完成的交易全部「作廢、取消並退款」。
面對法院命令，Kalshi 於 7 月 2 日向 CFTC 提出緊急申請，請求聯邦監管機關說明是否應執行州法院命令。
CFTC 最終要求 Kalshi 不得妥協，並在命令中指出，若開先例允許撤銷已執行的交易，「勢必會打擊公眾信心，讓交易者陷入恐慌，擔心今天執行的交易，會不會在一周或一年後莫名遭到撤銷」。

title: Iran threatens to block more trade routes as US launches fresh strikes
summary: US President Donald Trump vowed to strike Iran's bridges and power plants next week if the country does not return to talks.
full_text:
Iran threatens to block more trade routes as US launches fresh strikes
- Published
Iran has threatened to block further trading routes in the region, as the US launched a fresh wave of strikes on military targets.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards said the Strait of Hormuz would remain shut until the US ends its "acts of aggression" and said other regional oil and gas export channels could also be closed.
The warning came as the US military's Central Command (Centcom) said it had carried out drone, air and navy strikes on Iran on Wednesday morning, in addition to a seven-hour operation overnight.
US President Donald Trump vowed to strike Iran's bridges and power plants next week if the country does not return to talks.
"I'll save the energy targets for last, but ultimately we'll hit energy targets," Trump said in an interview on Special Report with Bret Baier that aired on Tuesday night.
The escalation in rhetoric comes after Trump said a 20% toll he had threatened to impose in the Strait of Hormuz would be replaced by "massive" trade and investment deals with Gulf states.
A renewed US blockade on Iranian ports was imposed on Tuesday evening, which stops vessels from transiting to and from Iranian ports and coastal areas.
In response, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) warned the US that it should "expect the closure of other oil and gas export routes that serve the interests of the United States and its allies". It did not elaborate on which routes could be affected.
Meanwhile, Iran's state-run broadcaster reported that the country's army had carried out separate attacks on US targets in Jordan, Kuwait and Bahrain.
The US allies also said they intercepted drones and missiles launched from Iran.

title: Travellers warned of methanol poisoning risks in new campaign
summary: Holidaymakers are urged to understand the dangers and symptoms of methanol poisoning.
full_text:
Travellers warned of methanol poisoning risks in new campaign
- Published
When Calum MacDonald visited a bar in Laos he experienced "a blinding kaleidoscopic light" permanently impairing his vision, less than two days after having a drink.
He was poisoned by methanol in 2024, and has since joined a UK government campaign, external to raise awareness of the risks that turned his life upside down.
MacDonald, who is in his 20s and from Surrey, told BBC Breakfast he was unaware of the dangers when travelling and if he had known "I probably would be in a different situation today".
Methanol is a highly toxic industrial strength form of alcohol that can sometimes be found in counterfeit, illegally produced or contaminated alcoholic drinks.
As little as 30ml - about a single shot - can be fatal to an adult, while smaller amounts can cause serious and permanent harm, including blindness.
Twenty-nine destinations now carry methanol poisoning warnings on UK government travel advice, including popular tourist destinations such as Indonesia, Laos and Vietnam.
Among those to die after consuming methanol was Margaret McKie's 38-year-old daughter Kirsty.
Kirsty, originally from Stockport, was living in Bali and engaged to a man who owned a wine business and restaurant, so was cautious about only buying alcohol from reputable suppliers.
"When Kirsty became ill it didn't occur to her for a second that [methanol poisoning] was what could be wrong," McKie told BBC Breakfast.
"She was fairly tired, she'd been working hard, she'd had a couple of drinks, she just thought she had a hangover, she didn't seek help and when she lost consciousness her fiance got her to the hospital and by that point it was too late to save her."
McKie argued it was important for people to not only be prevented from drinking alcohol laced with methanol but to also understand the symptoms to get help in time.
"Look out for your friends, if you notice a friend who seems more ill, get them help," McKie said.
Some of the symptoms of methanol poisoning can include:
- Vomiting, poor judgement, loss of balance and drowsiness are early signs 
- 12-48 hours after drinking symptoms can include abdominal pain, vertigo, hyperventilation, breathlessness, blurred vision and/or blindness, coma and convulsions 
- Vision issues are a distinctive red flag, particularly blurry vision, trouble looking at bright lights, and in some cases complete blindness. "Snowfield vision" (seeing snowy static like an old TV) or tunnel vision can also occur 
MacDonald also advised people look out for each other while travelling and to know the risks.
"Enjoy your travel but ultimately it's really important to have all the information that you possibly can before you do go to these places because I think ultimately it's very difficult to ultimately eliminate all risk," he said.
"If you have the information at hand and you can recognise situations in which you might be at higher risk and you can recognise the symptoms and then you can mitigate those risks and do the best you can to look after yourself and look after your friends."
Foreign Office minister Hamish Falconer said the government was using the campaign to amplify its own travel advice for people to check the Foreign Office's warnings.
Asked how this information reaches young people such as backpackers who may not be visiting government websites, Falconer said the campaign was using a range of ways.
"We're partnering with influencers on TikTok, YouTube, other influencer channels... we're trying to make sure that we get [the campaign] out through all the channels," Falconer said on BBC Breakfast.
"The campaigners and families have been working with other people too to try and make sure there's content out there so it's now in the PSHE [Personal, Social, Health and Economic education] curriculum, it's being pushed online, trying to make sure it gets wide reach."

title: UK's extreme weather is the new normal, Met Office says
summary: The latest report on the UK's climate warns cold mountainous areas are also being lost.
full_text:
Climate we had in 20th Century 'has now gone' - Met Office
- Published
Weather that was once considered extreme is becoming the "new normal", according to the latest Met Office report on the UK's climate.
It shows the hottest day of the year in the south of England is now typically 4.5C warmer than it was in 1961-1990.
The scientists say that the country's climate is "on the move" as northern areas of Britain now see warmer temperatures that used to only affect southern England.
Homes, schools, hospitals, and transport networks are struggling to cope with back-to-back heatwaves this summer, exposing how unprepared the UK is for climate change.
"We are right now living in a time of historic and unprecedented change, and in terms of temperature, on annual, seasonal, monthly and daily timescales, this evidence shows the climate of the 20th Century has now gone," said Mike Kendon, Met Office climate information scientist.
The report confirmed that 2025 was the warmest year on record since data began to be collected in 1884.
It highlighted that we are now experiencing the effects of climate change.
The decade 2016-2025 was 1.33C warmer than 1961-1990. Seemingly small increases in average temperatures can increase the likelihood of spikes in extreme temperatures.
The report focused on extremes in high temperatures because these often have the greatest impact on people.
The number of days over 30C and nights over 18C has more than quadrupled for Greater London in the period 2016-2025, compared to 1961-1990.
In the southeast of England, "we are seeing the emergence of new warmer climates", explains Kendon.
At the same time areas including Vale of York and Lancashire have similar temperatures now to those seen in Greater London in 1961-1990.
"Think of this warming as moving north and uphill," Kendon explains, highlighting that the UK is losing the coldest habitats from the tops of mountains.
The impacts of extreme heat have been seen this summer, as people in many parts of the UK experienced days of above-average temperatures and high humidity.
More than 2,700 people may have died from heat-related causes in England and Wales during the exceptionally hot weather in May and June, according to experts at Imperial College London, the Met Office and the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine.
The scientists also assessed availability of water in spring and summer, and drought frequency.
In spring 2025, most of England and Wales received less than half of the 1991-2020 average rainfall. England had its driest spring for over 100 years.
The total amount of water moving through rivers in England in March to August 2025 was the second lowest since 1961.
Climate change is expected to bring more severe winter rainfall and flooding in the UK, but hotter and drier summers are projected to bring more severe droughts in the future.
Lack of rainfall also affects soil and food production.
This year soils were drier than average for the time of year across central and southern England towards the end of June.
Plant growth can be stunted in dry soil, affecting animals or birds that rely on them for food or the success of a food crop.
Parched landscapes increase the risk of wildfires, and dry soil heats up more quickly and can amplify heatwaves.
- The UK's summers are getting hotter - but how prepared are we? - Published24 June

title: Three killed as Russian bombing of Odesa continues
summary: In recent days, Russia and Ukraine have launched attacks on each others' infrastructure for shipping goods.
full_text:
Three killed as Russian bombing of Odesa continues
- Published
Three people have been killed following an overnight Russian attack on the Black Sea port of Odesa, according to a local official.
Governor of Odesa region Oleh Kiper said the "massive" drone and missile strike marked the fifth day in which Russia has attacked the region.
The Russian ministry of defence said it had deliberately targeted port infrastructure, "used for the unloading of petroleum, oil, and lubricants".
The attacks come as European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen visits Kyiv to discuss co-operation between European and Ukrainian defence industries.
Writing on Telegram, Kiper accused Russia of deliberately targeting the civilian population, as well as industrial and port infrastructure in the area.
He said residents were killed and injured when a Russian missile struck a multi-storey residential building.
He added that a non-residential building and a gas pipeline were also hit.
In its statement, Russia claimed to have targeted sites involved in the manufacture of military hardware, and the transport of cargo.
Russia's attacks in recent days have targeted Ukraine's deepwater Black Sea ports in the wider Odesa area, which handle much of the country's grain and other cargo and are vital to its wartime economy.
Also overnight, Ukraine said its drones hit 20 Russian vessels in the Black Sea.
It follows intensive attacks on Russian ships in the Sea of Azov, which sits between Crimea, Ukraine's eastern coastline, and Russia.
The Ukrainian attacks have forced Russia, the world's top grain exporter, to restrict shipping in the Sea of Azov - a route that handles about a quarter of its grain exports, according to news agency Reuters.
As the attacks continue, Ukraine is attempting to navigate a tumultuous political situation which has seen President Volodymyr Zelensky dismissing Prime Minister Yulia Svyrydenko after less than a year in the post.
A motion to accept Svyrydenko's resignation was passed in Ukraine's parliament on Tuesday, despite some lawmakers questioning whether the reason for the change had been explained.
Serhiy Koretskyi, the head of state oil and gas firm Naftogaz, is seen as a likely successor to Svyrydenko, with parliament set to vote on the appointment on Thursday.
On Wednesday morning, Ursula von der Leyen arrived in Kyiv, writing on social media that it was a "special moment" and that it was her 11th visit to the country since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
She said the new initiatives she was set to announce would allow both sides to "produce more, and faster".

title: What happened to David Batty, who shook off penalty miss against Argentina?
summary: England midfielder David Batty quickly shook off his penalty miss against Argentina in 1998. As the two teams prepare to meet in the World Cup knockout stage again, BBC Sport asks: what happened to him?
full_text:
What happened to David Batty, who shook off penalty miss against Argentina?
- Published
Few players take their first penalty as a professional at a World Cup, but that was exactly the situation David Batty found himself in back in 1998.
England's breathless last-16 tie against Argentina had gone to a shootout and it fell to the midfielder to keep his side in the tournament with the fifth spot-kick.
The country held its breath as Batty stepped up, only for goalkeeper Carlos Roa to make the save to send Argentina through.
Rather than collapsing to the turf in tears, or pulling his shirt over his face, Batty held his head high.
When he emerged from the dressing room that night, he even questioned why his friend and agent, Hayden Evans, had come down from the stands to check on him.
It was as if nothing had happened.
It was only when a fast food company later wanted Batty to feature in an advert campaign making light of his penalty miss that he showed his feelings.
The angry Yorkshireman did not want to profit off the disappointment of those who had travelled out to the World Cup. No wonder he was a cult figure with supporters.
As England prepare to meet Argentina in the knockout stage of the World Cup once more, we revisit a piece about Batty's enduring popularity and his low-key retirement.
England v Argentina
Fifa World Cup 2026 semi-final
15 July, 20:00 BST
Watch live on BBC One and BBC iPlayer (UHD coverage available) from 19:00 BST. Listen to build-up and full match commentary on BBC Radio 5 Live and BBC Sounds from 18:00 BST. Follow TV and radio coverage, plus live text updates, in-play video clips, post-match highlights and analysis on the BBC Sport website and app.
'I don't think anyone has seen him since we played'
Dozens of phones buzzed across the globe last December.
Rio Ferdinand, Mark Viduka, Jason Wilcox, even former manager David O'Leary were among those alerted to new messages in their Leeds United WhatsApp group.
It was Batty's 57th birthday.
Only no-one who shared a dressing room with the ex-midfielder had the slightest idea where he was.
"I don't think anyone has seen him since we played together," Viduka said. "Everyone was wishing him happy birthday – but he's not even in the group."
To say Batty has kept a low profile since retiring in 2004 would be an understatement.
A series of amusing rumours have spread over the years as a result, amid claims Batty has become a superbike champion under a fake name, trained to be a master butcher and gone off grid to live in a caravan.
The reality is a little different, but this was someone who was never going to stay involved with the game.
Batty's agent, Evans, knew that better than most.
"It was clear from day one that he would never go into coaching, for example, and never seek that as a route back into football," he said.
"David has been as good as his word, which is him through and through.
"He always said, 'When I retire, that will be it. I won't have anything to do with the football industry'."
So just what happened to Batty?
A valued team-mate in title wins
It is a question that has been repeatedly asked.
Not least at the various reunions to mark Leeds' title triumph in 1992 or Blackburn Rovers' Premier League win three years later.
Batty was involved in both of those landmark achievements, but ex-Blackburn midfielder Mark Atkins has not caught up with him since their playing days.
"We have tried to get him to the dos we have had, but nobody can get hold of him," he said.
"He's not that type of person. Even if he was living five miles away, he wouldn't turn up because he's a very personal guy, really."
Aside from a rare trip to Elland Road to lay a wreath on the pitch in memory of his close friend Gary Speed, following his tragic death in 2011, Batty has tended to keep out of the public eye.
Viduka, who quietly opened a cafe in Croatia after hanging up his boots, can relate.
"In this day and age, everyone shows off everything they do in every moment, like what they had for breakfast," he said. "Who cares?
"If anyone was not going to be like that, it was Batts."
Rather than entertaining corporate guests, representing footballers or working in the media, Batty always planned to dedicate his time solely to his family in Yorkshire after retiring.
It has only added to the cult surrounding a player who former Leeds team-mate Eirik Bakke called one of his "heroes".
"If someone tackled you, Batts was always there to stand up for you," he said. "You don't find those types of players a lot. You could always rely on him."
Batty was more than a mere enforcer, however.
As well as standing his ground, and aggressively winning the ball back, the England international rarely gave away possession.
Those qualities quickly struck ex-Leeds midfielder John Sheridan, who was Batty's "mentor" in his early days at the club.
"You would think butter wouldn't melt in his mouth when you looked at him then," he said.
"But he was tough as nails. He made the game look very simple by doing the simple things easily."
'Not what you would expect from a multimillionaire footballer'
Batty also became a valued member of the various dressing rooms he inhabited.
Those who worked with him recall his dry sense of humour and practical jokes, the comparatively modest car he drove and how he did not get dragged down by the inevitable setbacks of the game.
Dave Hancock got to know Batty a little better than most as Leeds' head physiotherapist during the midfielder's gruelling rehabilitation from a career-threatening achilles injury in his second spell at Elland Road.
It was quickly apparent that he was not your typical Premier League footballer.
"In all my years in football, I don't think I've met a character like Batts," said Hancock, who also had spells with England and Chelsea.
"He was a talisman, for sure. A true, gritty Yorkshireman, who was very simple in his life with very simple pleasures. I don't think he ever went abroad [on holiday].
"He was not what you would expect from a multimillionaire footballer."
Those who encountered Batty at Blackburn and Newcastle felt similarly.
When Blackburn won the title, in 1995, for instance, Batty could not bring himself to pick up a medal after missing the majority of the season with a broken foot.
Batty instead felt for Atkins, who had filled in superbly during his absence, after his fellow midfielder was left out of the squad for the final fixture of the campaign against Liverpool.
"He was so supportive and felt sorry that he played the last couple of games instead of me," Atkins said.
"There was nothing against him when I got left out. It wasn't his fault. It was just the manager's decision, but there was a rumour going around that he didn't pick his medal up or left it somewhere.
"He shouldn't have because, whether he was injured or not, he was still a big part of the team."
A family man who chose the quiet life
Yet there is a reason you won't see Batty at the anniversary dinners to mark that title win.
Batty did not uproot during his time at Blackburn, or even when he made the switch to Newcastle in 1996.
He instead continued to commute from the family home in Yorkshire.
By the time his Newcastle team-mates were doing extras on the training field, Batty was often on his way out of the car park.
That image stuck with former Newcastle defender Warren Barton.
"He would already be in his car with his hand out the window, making a gesture to us," he said.
"When Saturday came, he was ready to go, but he loved being back home.
"He just wanted to come in, do his training and get back to his kids. We respected him for that."
It is why Barton always expected Batty to "sail into the sunset" in retirement.
So it proved after Batty chose to maintain a quiet family life after retiring.
This is a figure who is "peaceful in his own skin" in the words of Evans.
"He was then and is now a dedicated family man," he added. "He's very happy in his life as he sits right now.

title: Don't panic - five ways to stop your kids' endless scrolling
summary: Parenting experts share their tips on how to keep children's screen time under control.
full_text:
Don't panic - five ways to stop your kids' endless scrolling
- Published
If you're a parent, you may have breathed a sigh of relief - or perhaps frustration - at the UK government's plans to implement an overnight social media curfew for 16 and 17-year-olds.
It would see apps such as Instagram, TikTok and YouTube made unavailable by default to the teenagers - though they will be able to opt out of the curfew if they want.
Features the government considers addictive such as auto-play videos and infinite scrolling will also be disabled under the plans, aimed at improving teenagers' focus, sleep quality and family life.
We asked some parenting experts for their tips on how to pry those phones away from their offspring's hands – even if only for a short while.
1. Start small and be realistic
Many parents who have already given their children tablets or smartphones might wonder if the best thing is to just get rid of them. But that might not be the most productive option, believes child psychologist Dr Jane Gilmour.
"Changing a habit is always going to be hard," she says. Instead, she recommends implementing changes at a neutral moment, not in the heat of an argument about screen time. "Calm brains communicate best."
A good first step to reducing screen time could be designating a set place in the home for devices, such as a particular cupboard.
"Have one place for chargers... so when the phones go away, they go on the charger and that's it."
2. Be collaborative
Older children and teenagers can benefit from being part of the conversation around screen time, rather than having rules imposed on them, says child psychologist Dr Maryhan Baker.
Acknowledging the peer pressure surrounding social media can help get teens onside, she says, such as telling them: "I understand that that's where you connect with your friends. I understand the social pressure if you're deemed not to be on this. I really get it.
"So let's have a conversation about how we can begin to create space within our day, and your day where you're not on that phone all of the time."
Parenting coach Olivia Edwards adds that building a strong connection with your child or teenager will make it easier to regulate screen use.
"We have to have a strong relationship with our child because that is what's going to get us towards co-operation [and] teamwork."
This could include taking a genuine interest in the content your child consumes online.
3. Turn screen time into learning opportunities
Many parents feel they're struggling to keep up with the rapidly changing fads and trends on social media. But there is an opportunity for both adults and children to learn from each other through frank discussions about screen time.
Olivia says: "You might say something like: 'How do you think social media works? How do you think that app works to keep people looking at it? Did you know they make money off the more time people spend on it?'"
Jane also says parents can teach their children digital literacy in a hands-on way. "There might be content that you can look at together and say, 'OK, do you think that that is true? How would I figure out if that's true or not?'"
4. Model good behaviour
It's no secret that children mimic their parents, so encouraging good screen habits in them might have to start with some self reflection.
Maryhan encourages a light-hearted approach to this. "Even if we just do a slightly self-deprecating conversation with our kids, like: 'We're all guilty of this, I'm not as great on my relationship with [my phone] as I could be.'"
Phones and tablets have provided people of all ages with an ever-present source of entertainment, but Jane says that both adults and children could benefit from embracing boredom a bit more.
"Being on the screen, it keeps us looking at the external world. When we go into our internal world and we sort of stare into space, into the middle distance, it allows us to think about the past, it allows us to visualise the future, it predicts creativity.
"So when your kids are protesting [that] there's nothing to do, they're just staring into space - that's OK. And actually that's a positive thing."
5. Don't panic
Parenting has never been easy, but raising children in a time where screens are everywhere, while we are still learning how they affect us, can be very worrying.
Dr Tony Sampson, a reader in digital communication at the University of Essex, says parents shouldn't fall into the trap of moral panic.
"There is a tendency for anxious parents to become caught up in a prevailing media panic and see all adolescent brains as simply hardwired for social media addiction," he says.
But children and teenagers have what's called neuroplasticity – their brains are better at adapting and bouncing back than adults' brains.
"We read a lot about the ways in which social media erodes attention," he says.
"[But] social media does not shorten or erode attention. It captures it and diverts it toward engagement with commercial content.
"Positive technological use can help boost neuroplasticity for creativity, exploration and learning."

title: Several flights diverted after plane blocks Gatwick runway
summary: An Easyjet flight had to land at Stanstead Airport instead, but then became stuck there when it couldn't find fuel.
full_text:
Several flights diverted after plane blocks Gatwick runway
- Published
A number of flights were diverted from Gatwick airport after a plane temporarily blocked one of its runways.
Emergency services met the British Airways plane as a precaution upon landing, following reports of a "technical fault" with the aircraft.
One of the diverted planes, an already-delayed EasyJet flight from Rome to Gatwick, had to land at Stansted airport instead - and subsequently became stuck there because it was unable to find fuel.
Passengers were left on that plane for over two hours in the middle of the night before disembarking.
The BA plane which temporarily blocked the runway at Gatwick Airport reportedly experienced a landing gear issue. BA said the plane landed safely and passengers disembarked normally.
A London Gatwick spokesperson said: "Earlier this morning, the runway was closed for a short period due to a technical issue with an aircraft.
"As a result, a small number of flights were diverted, with the majority later returning to London Gatwick. As always, safety and security is our number one priority."
There were a number of delays to arrivals and departures from Gatwick Airport on Wednesday, although it was not clear if these were connected to the earlier runway closure.
- What are my rights if my flight is cancelled or delayed? - Published2 hours ago
 
EasyJet apologised "for the inconvenience caused by the diversion and delay in disembarking" its flight which was diverted to Stansted.
"While we worked to make onward arrangements for customers, as no ground handling staff were available for the unscheduled arrival, the aircraft was unable to refuel and so customers disembarked in Stansted and were advised they would be reimbursed for their onward travel," it said.
Passengers were informed EasyJet was struggling to get any fuel to the plane at Stansted. The airline has no arrangement with Swissport which had provided some fuel to another BA plane.
People on the plane got off at Stansted and had to make their own onward travel arrangements and claim back costs later.
Can I claim extra compensation for disruption?
In circumstances when flight disruption is considered to be the airline's fault, you have a number of rights under UK law., external
These apply as long as you are flying from a UK airport on any airline, arriving at a UK airport on an EU or UK airline, or arriving at an airport in the EU on a UK airline.
What you are entitled to depends on what caused the cancellation and how much notice you are given.
If your flight is cancelled with less than two weeks' notice, you may be able to claim compensation based on the timings of the alternative flight you are offered.
The amount you are entitled to also depends on how far you were travelling:
- for flights under 1,500km, such as Glasgow to Amsterdam, you can claim up to £220 per person 
- for flights of 1,500km to 3,500km, such as East Midlands to Marrakesh, you can claim up to £350 per person 
- for flights over 3,500km, such as London to New York, you can claim up to £520 per person

title: Cody Bellinger stars at MLB All-Star game, wins MVP award
summary: With his father - former big leaguer Clay Bellinger - in attendance, the New York Yankees player earned MVP honours.
full_text:
Cody Bellinger stars at MLB All-Star game, wins MVP award
With his father – former big leaguer Clay Bellinger – in attendance, the New York Yankees player earned MVP honours.
Cody Bellinger had a night for the ages.
His young daughters sat next to him and his father watched from the back of the room as he spoke about winning Major League Baseball’s (MLB) All-Star Game’s Most Valuable Player (MVP) award.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items- list 1 of 4‘Football is for everyone’: Djed Spence and the Three Lions’ Muslim moment
- list 2 of 4England and Argentina set for their first meeting in a World Cup semifinal
- list 3 of 4Photos: Spain ends Mbappe and France’s World Cup dream to reach final
- list 4 of 4VIDEO: Spain defeats France to reach FIFA World Cup final
“Just being able to hang out and watching him win an award, it’s pretty cool,” former Yankee Clay Bellinger said after his son’s two-run single in the first inning off Cristopher Sanchez started the American League to a 4-0 win on Tuesday night.
Cody re-signed with the Yankees last winter for a $162.5m, five-year deal and he has been a key part of the offence. He was hitting .280 through mid-June before a slump dropped his average to .254 heading into the All-Star break. Bellinger hasn’t homered in a month.
“Baseball is the craziest game in the world. It really is. Sometimes it’s unexplainable,” he said. “Going into the break, I actually was feeling pretty good. I felt like I was on the right track.”
Clay Bellinger was an outfielder and infielder for the Yankees from 1999 to 2001, winning a pair of World Series titles, and then finished his big league career with the Anaheim Angels in 2002.
Cody was five years old when his father won his second World Series title. Clay never imagined the player Cody would turn into.
“I knew he was good, but not this good,” Clay said.
‘Took a long time to get back’
Cody became the fourth Yankees player to win the All-Star Game MVP after Derek Jeter (2000), Mariano Rivera (2013) and Giancarlo Stanton (2022).
“Wearing this jersey – I feel proud wearing it,” he said. “It comes with a lot.”
Bellinger, who turned 31 on Monday, was a fourth-round draft pick by the Los Angeles Dodgers in 2013 and made the All-Star team in 2017, when he was voted NL Rookie of the Year. He hit 47 homers in 2019 and was voted the NL MVP after making his second All-Star team.
“I was, like, ‘Oh, I’ll be here every year,'” he said. “It took a long time to get back. It’s such a competitive league.”
He followed with three straight subpar seasons, missing time in 2021 because of calf, hamstring and rib injuries. He was cut after the 2022 season and signed a $17.5m, one-year deal with the Cubs.
Bellinger hit a career-high .307 with 29 homers and 97 RBIs, became a free agent again and signed an $80m, three-year contract with the Cubs. After a subpar, injury-slowed season, he was dealt to the Yankees.
He tested the free-agent market, then decided to stay in pinstripes.
“He loves it there,” Clay said. “He loves the teammates, loves the city, loves playing in Yankee Stadium. So, it was kind of a no-brainer.”
Daughters Caiden and Cy accompanied Cody onto the field along with his wife, Chase, for photos after he received his award from Hall of Famer Mike Schmidt.
“You always hope for your kids to do well, whether or not it’s playing baseball or doing whatever they like to do,” Clay said. “He’s been pretty good at it for quite a long time.”

title: Gibraltar border controls lifted: Is it part of Schengen, the UK – or both?
summary: A new treaty signed by Britain and the EU includes the removal of border checks between Spain and Gibraltar.
full_text:
Gibraltar border controls lifted: Is it part of Schengen, the UK – or both?
A new treaty signed by Britain and the EU includes the removal of border checks between Spain and Gibraltar.
Thousands of people who travel every day between the southern tip of Spain and the British territory of Gibraltar will no longer have to cross a physical border from Wednesday.
This came after the European Union and United Kingdom on Tuesday signed a treaty that delivers “economic and trade certainty for the people and businesses of Gibraltar, safeguards British sovereignty and protects the autonomous operation of UK military facilities”.
Recommended Stories
list of 4 items- list 1 of 4‘Brexit has not been the economic disaster many claimed’
- list 2 of 4Mapping the 10 countries with the most overseas territories
- list 3 of 4Andy Burnham in line to become British PM after securing party support
- list 4 of 4Murder of UK politician Ann Widdecombe was ‘targeted attack’, police say
The treaty was signed in Brussels by the European Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic, British Minister of State for Europe Stephen Doughty, Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares and Gibraltar Chief Minister Fabian Picardo.
“Gibraltar was left out of the UK-EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement following Brexit, creating the prospect of a devastating ‘hard border’ for the 15,000 people – more than half of Gibraltar’s workforce – who cross the land border between Spain and Gibraltar every day,” the treaty said.
Here’s what we know about the treaty:
What does the treaty include?
Britain secured Gibraltar, a strategically important enclave at the southern tip of Spain, in the 1713 Treaty of Utrecht, which ended the War of Spanish Succession.
The contested British overseas territory of 38,000 people is perched at a strategic location, only 8 nautical miles (15km) from Morocco where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Mediterranean Sea.
The new agreement allows residents of Gibraltar to cross into Spain using residence cards without needing to have their passports stamped. In return, Spanish citizens will be allowed to enter Gibraltar using a government ID card.
The treaty in effect brings Gibraltar into the EU’s Schengen free-travel area, which allows people from 29 countries to move among them freely without needing visas.
At Gibraltar’s airport and port, entry and exit checks will be conducted by both British and Spanish border officials. The arrangement is similar to what’s in place at Eurostar train stations in London and Paris, where both British and French officials check passports.
Travellers to Gibraltar from countries outside the Schengen area, including the UK, will have to contend with the EU Entry/Exit System, which was rolled out in Europe in April and replaced passport stamps with biometric data collected through photographs and digital fingerprints.
Under the older system, every person had to face two border checks, one by Gibraltarian border agents and the other by Spanish officials when entering or exiting the Schengen area. The checks caused long queues, heavily impacting the workers who made the crossing daily.
The British government said the agreement brings “fluidity for people and goods crossing the Gibraltar-Spain border to support economic growth and jobs in the region”.
What was the motivation behind the treaty, and how does Brexit feature in it?
In a 2016 referendum in which UK voters approved leaving the EU, 96 percent of voters on “the Rock”, as Gibraltar is popularly known in English, supported remaining in the bloc.
When Britain eventually left the EU in 2020, the relationship between Gibraltar and the bloc was left unresolved. Previous talks on a deal to ensure people and goods could keep flowing across the border had made halting progress.
While the Trade and Cooperation Agreement, which came into force in 2021, broadly covered relations between the bloc and Britain, it was decided that Gibraltar would be addressed in separate negotiations because of its unique situation because it’s not in the EU customs union or the Schengen area.
In 2025, the EU and UK announced an agreement on those issues after more than three and a half years of negotiations.
Does the treaty place Gibraltar in a special position, and do any other British overseas territories have the same privileges?
Yes, Gibraltar is in a unique position because it has now gained EU privileges without being an actual EU member.
Still, it is under British sovereignty, and the treaty solely seeks to resolve post-Brexit cooperation with the EU and border management due to its open land border with the EU.
None of Britain’s other overseas territories, which include 14 territories scattered across the Caribbean and the Antarctic, has a deal similar to Gibraltar’s due to the shared land border.
Some of the territories have international arrangements, including Bermuda, which has its own immigration and tax systems, and the Falkland Islands, which govern themselves.
